summary: Batch 8 of review-queue-next.json (the entries with batch field = 8: n 569, 570, 574, 576, 637, 638, 559, 571, 577, 578, 639, 641). Note: the file's batch field is 1-based; array index 8 is the batch with field 9 (only 2 entries, 643 and 651), so I took the batch whose field is 8, which has the stated 12 entries. All 12 fetched live with an honest User-Agent, robots.txt checked per host, at most 1 request/second/host, no browser, nothing under legacy/, tools/t0, tests/t0, ops, baseline, release and no repo files written (work in the scratchpad only). Tally: 11 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY, 1 REJECT (576), 0 APPROVE for the verbatim quote corpus, 0 NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW. Rights: 2 at tier A1 (559 NPS text, 574 OR vol. 27 pt. 2 scan; both link-out only for value or duplication reasons, not rights), 1 A1 for a rejected wrong-volume item (576), 9 at tier C. Key findings: (1) entry 576 links to Series I vol. 26 part 2 (Confederate correspondence, West Florida to New Mexico, GPO 1889) and not to a full series or to anything about Gettysburg. (2) Entry 559 names Sallie Broadhead but the NPS page profiles Sallie Myers (nine civilians, no Broadhead, no outbound links). (3) Entry 571's claim that many journal articles cover Gettysburg is overstated (about 4 of 60 titles name Gettysburg). (4) Entry 639 is filed under Part X but describes itself as the finding aid for Part IX and does match the Carlisle items 586-591. (5) The Civil War Cycling indexes (577, 578) are complete (378 and 211 numbered rows = 589 reports) and agree with our OCR index on first page for 568 of 583 comparable rows, but are copyright (all rights reserved) and carry typos. Not verified: UNT's own terms-of-use page (behind an ALTCHA challenge I did not solve), direct Cupola PDF downloads (Cloudflare challenge, not circumvented; two PDFs read via Wayback captures instead), the Gettysburg Magazine issue date for 637 (issue number from the gdg.org contents page, year only from a web search), HathiTrust/eHistory links (never fetched), and the Valley of the Shadow TEI source file.
systemic_findings: Batch numbering: review-queue-next.json uses 1-based batch fields. Index 8 of the batches array is batch field 9 (2 entries); the 12-entry batch the task describes is the one with field 8, and that is the one reviewed. Any other verifier reading by array index will review the wrong entries.

Wrong-target link pattern: entry 576 claims a full series but the identifier (warofrebellion012602rootrich) decodes to series 01, volume 26, part 02. Worth auditing every Part VIII/XII entry whose identifier or title implies a whole set, and any other Archive identifier, against the item's own title page.
Part placement: entry 639 is in Part X (African Americans in the invasion) while its own description says it is the finding aid used to build Part IX; its member list matches entries 586-591.

Third-party hosts add bot defences even where robots.txt allows: Cupola PDFs (Cloudflare challenge on viewcontent.cgi) and the UNT rights page (ALTCHA). Neither was circumvented; Wayback captures of the PDFs served as allowed alternatives. UNT robots.txt disallows the ClaudeBot user agent entirely and sets a 3-second crawl delay, which matters for any product that fetches under a Claude-branded agent.

Rate limiting is shared: archive.org (including the Wayback availability API) returned HTTP 429 after short bursts while this batch ran, which suggests other workflows share the same IP. The 1 request/second/host rule is per process, so parallel verifiers can exceed it in total; space Archive calls out.

The Civil War Cycling OR indexes (577, 578) have page-range differences against our OCR index (15 of 583 comparable first pages) plus typos (No. 5l7, No 520, No. 524 link 'http://z', No. 471 pages '74-476'). If the list took its page ranges from these pages, those errors flow into the 39 OR ranges the registry already flags as different.

None of this batch's entries are usable for the verbatim quote corpus. Modern articles and index pages are tier C (copyright reserved, no open licence found), and the two public-domain items are duplicates of text we already ingest or a short secondary summary.

items.written: 2011 (Vol. 2, Article 5); Cupola metadata gives online date 2013-05-08; subject is the July 1913 reunion
items.rights_basis: No open licence found. Cupola journal policies page: the author retains copyright and grants the Civil War Institute and The Cupola a non-exclusive licence; 'contents of this journal are protected by copyright'. The PDF cover page says only 'open access'. A search of all 14 volume pages, this article page and the About page for creativecommons or licence text found nothing. Free to read, not free to reuse.
items.evidence: Fetched the entry link (issue page /gcjcwe/vol2/iss1/, HTTP 200): it lists Evan Preston's article as one of four articles in Vol. 2 (2011). Fetched the article landing page /vol2/iss1/5/ (301 then 200): document type Article, citation 'The Gettysburg College Journal of the Civil War Era: Vol. 2, Article 5' (2011), abstract on the 50th-anniversary reunion and the absence of Black veterans from the white reconciliation message. The direct PDF (viewcontent.cgi?article=1018) answered HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge header, which I did not circumvent; instead I read the Internet Archive capture of that same PDF (2024-07-26, 22 pages, printed pages start at 66): it is built around the Reardon / Blight / Weeks dispute over whether Black veterans attended, Walter Blake's travel narrative Hand Grips, and Chicago Defender coverage of July 1913, and it concludes (footnotes to 179) that organized invitation or attendance is improbable. Description claim 'memory study of the reunion and the exclusion of Black veterans' checked: matches the abstract and conclusion; 'link is to the issue page' also true.
items.extraction_notes: Do not ingest text. Link out to the article page https://cupola.gettysburg.edu/gcjcwe/vol2/iss1/5/ (more precise than the issue page the entry uses). Direct PDF links are behind a bot challenge; if a copy is ever needed it requires the journal's permission or a human download. Facts only (reunion 1913, argument that no documented Black attendance) and no battle content.
issues: Entry link goes to the issue page, not the article page (/vol2/iss1/5/).
Direct PDF download returns a Cloudflare challenge to automated clients (not circumvented).
'Exclusion' is the author's inference from absence of evidence; the article argues improbability of invitation and attendance, it does not document an exclusion rule.
Commemoration of 1913, nothing about the July 1863 fighting.

items.written: 2014 (Vol. 4, Article 8); interview after Hartwig's retirement in fall 2013
items.rights_basis: No open licence found. Same Cupola policy as entry 569: the author keeps copyright, the journal holds a non-exclusive licence, contents are protected by copyright. The interviewee's own answers are also his words (not a US government work).
items.evidence: Fetched the entry link (issue page /gcjcwe/vol4/iss1/, HTTP 200): Vol. 4 (2014) lists 'An Interview with D. Scott Hartwig' by Thomas E. Nank '16 under the heading Interview. Fetched the landing page /vol4/iss1/8/ (301 then 200): the abstract says Hartwig, Supervisory Historian for Gettysburg National Military Park, retired in fall 2013 and Associate Editor Thomas Nank interviewed him about three decades of experience at Gettysburg and the future of the NPS and public history. Direct PDF blocked by Cloudflare challenge (403); I read the 2024-07-07 Internet Archive capture instead: 21 PDF pages, printed pages 89 to 107, question-and-answer format; questions cover teaching Pickett's Charge to students, NPS challenges, one on Capt. Johnston's reconnaissance near Round Top, Hartwig's plans and advice to young historians. Both description claims (interview; longtime park historian) are supported.
items.extraction_notes: Do not ingest. A modern interview about interpretation and the NPS, with one battle-related question; no new battle evidence. Link out to https://cupola.gettysburg.edu/gcjcwe/vol4/iss1/8/ if cited at all.
issues: Link is to the issue page, not the interview page.
Direct PDF download is behind a Cloudflare challenge.
Almost entirely about public history and park interpretation, not about the battle (tangential).
Classed as a scholarly source in Part VII, but the genre is an interview, not a peer-reviewed research article.

items.rights_basis: US Government publication (War Department, compiled by Lt. Col. R. N. Scott, Government Printing Office, 1889). Imprint year read from the scan itself: UNT OCR text of image 1 gives Series I, Volume XXVII, in three parts, Part II Reports, Washington, GPO, 1889. UNT item metadata sets dc:rights to Public Domain. UNT's own 'Responsibilities of Use / Licensing' page sits behind an ALTCHA proof-of-work challenge that I did not solve, so UNT's terms for its images and OCR text could not be read.
items.evidence: Fetched the entry link (HTTP 200): title The War of the Rebellion ... Series 1, Volume 27, In Three Parts. Part 2, Reports; 1,118 pages; creator US War Department; compiler Robert N. Scott; publisher GPO, Washington; date 1889; call number W 45.5; provider UNT Libraries Government Documents Department; one of 198 items in the series. Read OCR text of image 1 (title page as above), image 5 (page header 'Chap. XXXIX / The Gettysburg Campaign', summary of principal events June 3 to Aug 1, 1863) and image 293: printed page 293 begins No. 426, reports of Gen. Robert E. Lee, matching our OCR index (report 426, pages 293-326), so image number equals printed page at both spots checked. Description 'second independent scan of the Confederate reports volume' is accurate, with the nuance that Part 2 opens with 45 Federal supporting reports before the 166 Confederate ones. robots.txt: Crawl-delay 3, Request-rate 1/3, Disallow /stats/, /feedback/, */zoom/, and the ClaudeBot user agent is disallowed entirely (my QC agent uses its own name).
items.extraction_notes: No new text: the historian already ingests the same volume from Internet Archive (warofrebellion272unit). UNT offers per-page OCR as HTML at /ark:/67531/metapth154598/m1/N/ocr/ (about 590 KB per page, crawl-delay 3 s), so bulk extraction would be slow and is unnecessary. Use as a link-out scan and an independent page-image check for OR 27 part 2 only. Any Claude-named crawler would be refused by UNT's robots.txt.
issues: UNT 'citation / rights' page is behind a bot challenge (ALTCHA); not solved.
Item metadata carries an ISBN and LCCN (catalogue data that look like they come from a modern reprint record), but the OCR title page and Chap. XXXIX header read as the 1889 GPO original.
Volume duplicates the already-ingested Internet Archive OCR; adds a scan, not text.
UNT robots.txt disallows ClaudeBot.

items.written: 1889 (title page of this volume; the Archive's date field '1880-1901' is the span of the whole series)
items.rights_basis: US Government publication, GPO 1889 (title page text read from the Archive's OCR). Archive metadata: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT, copyright-region US, evidence note 'no visible notice of copyright ... stated date is 1889; published by the US government'. The rights are fine, but the item is the wrong work for this entry.
items.evidence: Fetched archive.org/metadata/warofrebellion012602rootrich (HTTP 200): title The War of the Rebellion ..., volume field 'Ser. 1 vol. 26:2', 648 images, University of California Libraries copy, date field 1880-1901, collection pub_official-records-of-union-and-confederate-armies. Fetched the first 60 KB of its OCR text: title page reads Series I, Volume XXVI, in two parts, Part II, Correspondence Confederate, Washington GPO 1889, and the first document set is Confederate correspondence, orders and returns relating to operations in West Florida, southern Alabama, southern Mississippi, Louisiana, Texas and New Mexico, May 14 to Dec 31, 1863 (Port Hudson headquarters orders of May 14, 1863). So the link is one volume out of about 128, not 'the full OR series', and it is not a Gettysburg volume (those are Ser. I vol. 27 parts 1-3). The description claim 'full-text download' is true only for this single volume (djvu.txt is about 2.2 MB, PDF about 67 MB).
items.extraction_notes: Do not use this link for Gettysburg. The correct Gettysburg scans are Ser. I vol. 27 pts. 1-3, already ingested: archive.org/details/warofrebellion271unit, 272unit, 273unit (I fetched their metadata: v.27:1, v.27:2, v.27:3, University of Illinois copies, 1190, 1132 and 1256 images). If a series-level link is wanted, use the Archive collection page given as replacement_url.
issues: Wrong volume: Ser. 1 vol. 26 pt. 2 (Confederate correspondence, Gulf and Trans-Mississippi theatres, May to Dec 1863), not the full series.
No Gettysburg content in this volume.
The Archive's date field is the series span 1880-1901; the volume itself is 1889.
Overlaps catalogue SRC-01 only at the series level; the entry's own identifier cannot serve as a series pointer.

items.written: Gettysburg Magazine issue 24 (2001 per a web search result; the gdg.org copy shows no issue or year; Word file created 2002-07-03)
items.rights_basis: Rights held by the publisher. The gdg.org Gettysburg Magazine contents page (same host, fetched) states that Morningside House, Inc. retains the rights to all articles reprinted by the Gettysburg Discussion Group. The article page itself has no licence. Copy hosted by a third party (gdg.org), plain http only.
items.evidence: Fetched the entry URL over http (HTTP 200, 200 KB, last-modified 2010-09-04; robots.txt 404 so no restrictions): title and author match (Peter C. Vermilyea, 'The Effect of the Confederate Invasion of Pennsylvania on Gettysburg's African American Community'); about 89 footnotes; it opens with Elizabeth ('Old Liz') Butler. Fetched http://www.gdg.org/Gettysburg%20Magazine/gcontents.html: it lists this article last under 'Issue Number 24' of Gettysburg Magazine, before 'Issue Number 25'. Checked two concrete claims in the text: (a) flight: a section on the exodus of Gettysburg's Black residents northward as Lee's army approached, with named examples (Biggs left on July 1); (b) capture: Confederate seizure of Black residents (e.g. the June 16 capture of 30-40 women and children at Chambersburg freed at Greencastle), and Butler bound and gagged, then escaping. Also reports the 1860 and 1870 census change (186 Black residents in 1860, no more than 74 still there in 1870) and the burial work done by Basil Biggs after the battle. The entry's note that the magazine is edited but not formally peer-reviewed is consistent with the venue (not independently verified).
items.extraction_notes: Do not ingest (publisher keeps rights). Cite as: Vermilyea, Gettysburg Magazine no. 24 (2001), copy at gdg.org; confirm the year and page range against the publisher before citing. Useful facts to look up elsewhere: the census figures and named individuals, each with footnotes to ACHS files, the 1860/1870 census, the Gettysburg Compiler, OR ser. 1 vol. 27 and Moore's Rebellion Record, which can be traced to primary sources.
issues: The page does not state issue, year or pagination; the entry gives none either. Issue 24 comes from the gdg.org contents page; the year 2001 comes only from a web search result.
Link is plain http (no https redirect seen).
Third-party reprint hosted without a permission notice other than the contents-page statement that Morningside House retains rights.
Not formally peer-reviewed.

items.rights_basis: No licence or copyright statement found on the post or on the blog's About page (both fetched, searched for copyright, licence, permission, creative); default copyright of the author and Dickinson College applies. House Divided site has no robots.txt (404).
items.evidence: Fetched the entry URL (HTTP 200, 74 KB). Page title 'The Slave Hunt: Amos Barnes and Confederate Policy', 'Posted by Cooper Wingert', dated 5 Jun 2018, on Blog Divided of the House Divided Project (Dickinson College); the URL slug uses an older working title ('confederate captures of African Americans'). Content: Confederate seizure of free Black Pennsylvanians in June 1863, Rachel Cormany and Philip Schaff witness accounts, Chambersburg and Mercersburg, the case of Amos Barnes sent to Castle Thunder in Richmond and released on Dec 14, 1863 by order of Assistant Secretary of War John A. Campbell, plus 12 numbered notes and a 'Primary Sources' list. Two description claims checked: 'footnoted essay' (12 notes) and 'assembling primary evidence on seizure of free Black Pennsylvanians' (primary-source list, Barnes/Creigh/Moore letters cited from archives). Part of the post is on the aftermath (camp slaves, Black Confederates myth).
items.extraction_notes: Do not ingest. Use as a map to primary evidence: Rachel Cormany diary (Valley of the Shadow FD1006), Franklin Repository, Schaff diary in Old Mercersburg (HathiTrust), Hoke's books, OR ser. 2 vol. 6 pp. 704-705, Castle Thunder records. Several of its links point to Perseus (robots Disallow) and HathiTrust (blocked), so they are not checkable by us.
issues: Blog post, not a journal article; listed in Part X among 'sources cited by House Divided'.
No licence statement anywhere on the site pages checked.
Slug differs from the displayed title.
Mostly the campaign (June 1863) and Richmond imprisonment, little about the July 1-3 battle.

items.written: Page footer: last updated May 5, 2015 (modern NPS text)
items.rights_basis: Text of an NPS page. The NPS disclaimer page (fetched) says material created by the NPS on its websites is generally in the public domain under 17 USC 105 unless otherwise indicated, and that some content is third-party (one image on this page is credited to ACHS). Treat the text as A1 and exclude the images.
items.evidence: Fetched the entry URL (home.nps.gov, HTTP 200; robots allow). The page profiles nine people: John Burns, Elizabeth Salome (Sallie) Myers, Daniel Skelly, Tillie Pierce, Jennie Wade, David McConaughy, David Wills, Dr. J.W.C. O'Neal, David Kendlehart. There is no Sallie Broadhead anywhere in the HTML (searched 'broadhead': zero hits); the description's 'Sallie Broadhead' is a different person from the page's Sallie Myers. The page names a published account only for Skelly (1932, 'A Boy's Experiences During the Battle of Gettysburg'), Pierce ('What a Girl Heard and Saw at the Battle') and O'Neal's grave journal; the content area has no outbound links at all, so it is not a finding aid to the primary texts. Descriptions of the nine are brief biographical paragraphs with minor typos.
items.extraction_notes: Short overview (about 1,000 words) of nine Gettysburg civilians; no primary text to extract. Use it only to cross-check names and roles, and look up each person's own account elsewhere (Skelly 1932, Pierce 1889 article, Myers diary). Do not rely on it as a witness list for Broadhead.
issues: Description names Sallie Broadhead; the page has Sallie Myers instead and no Broadhead.
'Published accounts each left' overstated: only Skelly and Pierce (and O'Neal's grave journal) are tied to named accounts; no links.
Placed under Part VI Civilian accounts but is a secondary overview, not a witness account.
Image credit to a third party (ACHS) means images are not covered by the public-domain statement.

items.written: Journal founded 2010; 14 volumes 2010-2025 (Vol. 14 is the current volume)
items.rights_basis: Journal-level: policies say the journal is open access but 'protected by copyright; users agree to abide by U.S. copyright law'; authors keep copyright; no Creative Commons or other licence found on the home page, the About page, 16 issue pages or two article pages.
items.evidence: Fetched the entry URL (HTTP 200) and the contents pages of all 14 volumes (/gcjcwe/volN/iss1/). Home page says open access, peer-reviewed, undergraduate journal; ISSN online 2165-3666. Counted 60 content items (articles, book reviews, one interview; front matter and editors' letters excluded). By title, four name Gettysburg: Vol. 2 reunion article (entry 569), Vol. 3 'Culp's Hill: Key to Union Success at Gettysburg', Vol. 6 'The Devan Family of Gettysburg', Vol. 10 'Examining the Falsehoods of Joshua Lawrence Chamberlain at Gettysburg'; two more touch Gettysburg (Vol. 4 Hartwig interview, Vol. 9 Camp Letterman and medical dissection), about 6 of 60, only 2 or 3 about the fighting itself. Titles only; abstracts not read for the rest. So 'many include Gettysburg topics' is an overstatement: a handful do.
items.extraction_notes: A journal home page: nothing to ingest. Member items of interest to Gettysburg: vol3 #7 (Culp's Hill), vol6 #6 (Devan family, Black civilians), vol9 #3 (Camp Letterman), vol10 #4 (Chamberlain at Gettysburg), vol2 #5 and vol4 #8 (entries 569, 570). Each needs its own review; PDF downloads are behind a Cloudflare challenge.
issues: 'Many include Gettysburg topics' is overstated (about 6 of 60 items, 4 by title).
All items are copyrighted by their undergraduate authors; open access is not a licence.
PDF downloads from cupola.gettysburg.edu are behind a bot challenge.
Entries 566-570 are items inside this journal (work group gcjcwe-journal).

items.rights_basis: The page footer reads Copyright (c) 2017-2026 Sue Thibodeau, all rights reserved, no part of the site to be reproduced without written permission. The page says the report names and titles are taken from the OR without edits and are in the public domain, but the compilation, the page ranges, the asterisk ratings (taken from B. Dixon's guide) and the layout are the site's. robots.txt allows the page (Disallow only /wp-admin/, /wp-includes/, /cgi-bin/, /author/).
items.evidence: Fetched the entry URL (HTTP 200, 379 KB): title 'Gettysburg Federal Officer Reports - Index to Vol. 27 Pt. 1' by Civil War Cycling, reports by number (1-378) and by officer name, every row linking to HathiTrust page images (Cornell copy coo.31924077699761, the same volume id as our manifest). I parsed the by-number table and compared it with our independent OCR index (historian-src/corpus/or27/reports.json): all 378 report numbers are present (No. 107 has an http link; No. 161 is absent from our OCR index and was confirmed earlier through the contents list). Of 376 comparable rows, first page agrees for 366; 10 differ (8 by one page, No. 134 by two, No. 10 by thirteen: '155-170' against OCR page 168). The entry's description (index used to build Parts I-III; by number and by name) is accurate.
items.extraction_notes: Do not copy the table. Our own OCR index is the independent derivation; use this page only as a human link-out and a cross-check (the 10 first-page differences are likely index typos, not errors in the scan). All its links go to HathiTrust, which blocks bots (not fetched).
issues: Copyright all rights reserved: link-out only.
About 10 of 376 first pages differ from the OCR index; a 'No. 10' page range looks like a typo.
Index covers reports only, not correspondence (the page says so).
All target links are HathiTrust, not checkable by us.

items.written: Page dated May 19, 2025; footer 'Last Update: June 7, 2025'
items.rights_basis: Same as entry 577: Copyright (c) 2017-2026 Sue Thibodeau, all rights reserved, no reproduction without written permission; only the OR names and titles are stated to be public domain.
items.evidence: Fetched the entry URL (HTTP 200, 275 KB): title 'Gettysburg Confederate Officer Reports - Index to Vol. 27 Pt. 2'; says OR 27 part 2 has 1,118 pages and begins with 45 Federal reports followed by 166 Confederate reports, and indexes report Nos. 379-589 (Federal 379-423, Confederate 424-589). Description 'Companion index for Reports 379-589' is exact. Parsed by-number table against our OCR index: 207 of 211 rows parsed automatically, the other 4 are malformed rows I found by hand (No. 471 pages printed as '74-476', No. 517 typed '5l7' with a lowercase L, No. 520 typed 'No 520' with no period, No. 524 with a broken link 'http://z'), so all 211 numbers are present. First page agrees with our OCR index for 202 of 207 rows; 5 differ by one page (Nos. 490, 502, 503, 513, 545). HathiTrust volume id coo.31924077728255 matches our manifest.
items.extraction_notes: Link-out and cross-check only; do not copy the table. If used to cross-check our OCR index, expect the typos listed in issues. Note it also lists Federal reports 379-423 (supporting armies) before the Confederate ones, so 'Confederate' in the title is not the whole of the range.
issues: Title says Confederate, but numbers 379-423 are Federal (45 reports).
Typos: No. 471 page range, No. 517 and No. 520 labels, No. 524 placeholder link (http://z).
5 of 207 first pages differ from the OCR index by one.
Copyright all rights reserved.

items.rights_basis: No licence or copyright statement found on the post or About page (searched); default copyright of the author and Dickinson College applies to the page's own text. The cited sources have their own status (many 1863-era texts are public domain, but that must be decided per item).
items.evidence: Fetched the entry URL (HTTP 200, 69 KB): 'Beyond Gettysburg: Primary Sources for the Gettysburg Campaign' by Cooper Wingert, posted June 11, 2018 on Blog Divided. It says he assembled digitized primary sources from the House Divided Project, the Dickinson College Archives, the Cumberland County Historical Society and his book, and groups them under: Confederate occupation of Carlisle (June 27-28), York and Wrightsville, Sporting Hill (June 30), Shelling of Carlisle (July 1-2), then Union, Confederate and civilian sources. I extracted 48 list items with 56 outbound links: archives.dickinson.edu 14, books.google.com 11, housedivided pages 12, HathiTrust 2, Cornell 2, one each for Perseus, Chronicling America, Internet Archive and about a dozen others. The list contains the Polk letter, the supply requisition, General Orders No. 72, the Underwood and Watson letters and the young girl's pocket diary, matching entries 586-591, which supports the description 'finding aid used to build Part IX'. One member link on archives.dickinson.edu (the supply requisition) returned 301 to https then 404, consistent with the earlier finding that those links are dead.
items.extraction_notes: Mine for leads, not text. 14 of the 56 links are on archives.dickinson.edu and appear dead at the old paths (one tested: 404); one points to Perseus (robots Disallow, do not fetch); 11 go to Google Books. Re-resolve Dickinson items through the Wayback Machine or the current Dickinson site and review each separately.
issues: Filed under Part X (African Americans in the invasion) but the entry itself says it is the finding aid used to build Part IX; the page has little about African Americans.
Many member links are dead (archives.dickinson.edu) or restricted for bots (Perseus, HathiTrust).
Campaign context (Carlisle, York, Sporting Hill, Harrisburg defenses), not the three-day battle.

items.written: Diaries of 1863 (collection page on the 'New American History' edition of the Valley of the Shadow; page itself undated)
items.rights_basis: Valley of the Shadow copyright statement (fetched): the site is freely available for non-commercial uses in research, teaching, scholarship and private study, users are responsible for their uses, and some materials may still be under copyright. The footer links to Creative Commons BY-NC 4.0. The 1863 diary text may be public domain, but the site's transcription, notes and the non-commercial term mean the member diaries need a human or counsel decision before any reuse.
items.evidence: Fetched the entry URL (HTTP 200; robots.txt is 404): page heading 'Samuel and Rachel Cormany (1863)', with a biography (Rachel born Canada 1836, Samuel born 1838 in Chambersburg, married 1860, Samuel enlisted in the 16th Pennsylvania Cavalry in Sept 1862) and two excerpt descriptions: Samuel's diary of service in the 16th Pennsylvania Cavalry in the campaign and the battle, and Rachel's diary of Chambersburg in June and July 1863. Description claim checked on the member page /diaries/FD1007 (Franklin County: Diary of Samuel Cormany (1863)): seven dated entries June 30 to July 6, 1863; entries for July 2 and 3 describe fighting, picket duty and the cannonade, with editor footnotes (note 5 says he fought most of July 2 beside infantry on the Union right; note 7 says the 16th Pennsylvania pursued the retreat toward Chambersburg). Rachel's diary is /diaries/FD1006 (entry 640). The page lists a TEI source file at api.valley.newamericanhistory.org (not fetched).
items.extraction_notes: Collection page only: nothing to ingest here. Member items: Samuel Cormany diary https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/diaries/FD1007 (June 30-July 6, 1863, with 'Original' and 'Modern Spelling' views) and Rachel's FD1006. TEI XML per diary exists at api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/papers/FD1007.xml (a different host; robots not checked, not fetched). Review each diary separately for provenance and rights before use.
issues: Rights unresolved for member diaries: site terms are non-commercial and it warns some material may be copyrighted; the project must decide whether non-commercial terms are acceptable.
Source of the transcription is not credited on the page (whether from the manuscript or a 1980s printed edition is not stated).
Whether the diary entries were written daily or later is not stated; the July 2 entry's account of Stuart carries an editor's explanation, so treat dating with care.
Entry 641 title says 'collection page' and class index: not itself a writing.

summary: Batch 6 (queue file batch number 7, 12 entries: 626, 629, 634, 560-568), each checked with real fetches at 1 request per second per host or slower. 3 APPROVE (626, 629, 634 and 565 are the primary or pre-1931 texts: 4 APPROVE in total), 7 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (560, 561, 563, 564, 566, 567, 568), 1 NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW (562), 0 REJECT. Correction to the first count: APPROVE = 626, 629, 634, 565 (4). What the 4 approvals rest on: 626 was read in the Internet Archive scan of the same Library of Congress copy (same ark as the HathiTrust id); 629 was read in the OCR and the page image of OR Ser. II vol. 6 (UC scan on the Archive); 634 was read in the Library of Congress OCR and a cropped page image through LoC's documented JSON and text services; 565 was read in the Archive scan of PMHB vol. 33. Real list errors found: 629 prints the name as Amos Bares, not Barnes, and the order never says Castle Thunder; 626's date range is too narrow and the diary never names McNeill's Rangers; 634's 'camp slaves' is the list's gloss (the printed line says the seven men were in uniform and accoutred as soldiers); 565 omits the author (Maj. William H. Lambert) and the subtitle; 562 bundles two articles under a link that looks like the issue front matter. Nothing in the six journals.psu.edu links could be fetched by me (connection reset on robots.txt, 3 attempts), so those links are unverified; their bibliographic data are confirmed from OpenAlex and the Internet Archive's own Pennsylvania History volume indexes, and two issues (1938, 1958) were read in Archive OCR. summary: Batch 0 (entries 545-551, 635, 553, 554, 557, 558): 10 APPROVE (all with a fetched, matching source; A1), 2 NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW (549: title names a series heading that is in SHSP vol. 4, not vol. 5, and it is a whole volume; 558: the Gutenberg text is the 24th edition (1969, (c)1935) whose public-domain status is only the host's claim), 0 REJECT. Perseus (www.perseus.tufts.edu) was not fetched (robots.txt: Disallow: / for * and for the Claude agents); every SHSP entry was verified on the University of Florida Internet Archive scans (volume-year metadata and 'Out of copyright' status) by reading the actual articles in the OCR text. Three SHSP entries (546, 547, 551's Doles report) reprint reports that are already in OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 2 (confirmed against the OR OCR): no new text. Fremantle's listed Google Books link opens a 2008 Applewood reprint; the original-imprint scans were found and read. 553 and 554 are the same 1908 Wisconsin printing by two routes. Not verified: Perseus page content, the Stanford renewal database (bot-challenged, not circumvented), Pierce's age, SHSP 31's year of the Times-Dispatch reprint beyond inference.
systemic_findings: All 7 SHSP entries (545-551) can be verified and later extracted from the University of Florida Internet Archive scans, which carry an explicit volume-and-year field and 'Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright': vol.4 southernhistoric4187sout, vol.5 southernhistoric5187sout, vol.6 southernhistoric6187sout, vol.7 southernhistoric7187sout, vol.8 southernhistoric8188sout, vol.13 southernhistoric1318sout, vol.31 southernhistoric3119sout (entries 544, 552 are vols. 7 and 37; vols. 7, 8, 13 and 31 are not among the ids the plan's SRC-08 lists). Perseus was not fetched: its robots.txt (read 2026-10-01) allows only /hopper/grants, research, about, collections and index.html for all agents and disallows everything else, including the Claude agents by name.

SHSP often reprints reports already in OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 2: Johnson (No. 481) and Heth (No. 549) in entry 546, Blackford (No. 527) in 547, Doles (No. 514) in 551 and the other brigade reports in vol. 8. Texts compared: identical apart from orthography. These add no new text; the new material in the SHSP entries is McLaws (545), Bright (548), Fitz Lee (550), Palfrey and Lane's brigade history (551).

The Archive's djvu OCR misreads digits and dates even in good scans: vol. 8 p. 41 reads 'July 10th, 1S(;3' where the page image reads 'July 19th, 1863'; vol. 31's newspaper year reads '190J'. Verbatim checks need the page image (https://archive.org/download/<id>/page/n<leaf>_w900.jpg works with the polite client; vol. 8 leaf = printed page + 9).
Entry 549's title does not belong to the volume it names (series heading in SHSP vol. 4, Oct. and Dec. 1877, not vol. 5). A title-versus-contents check on the other volume entries is worth running.

Entries 553 (Gutenberg #33121) and 554 (IA battleofgettysburg00haskuoft) are the same 1908 Wisconsin History Commission printing; sampled fragments of the two agree. The 1908 text itself reprints an undated c. 1878 pamphlet, not a manuscript; the registry description 'letter-length' understates a 37,000-word narrative.

Fremantle: the listed Google Books link opens a 2008 Applewood reprint; original-imprint scans exist (IA 1864 Bradburn, IA/Gutenberg Blackwood 1863). The book is mostly not about Gettysburg (Gettysburg days are about pp. 250-280 of the 1864 edition).

Tool note: tools/sources-qc/lib/http.mjs caches 5xx responses, so a transient gutenberg.org 503/504 (seen several times in this run) or an archive.org 500 stays in the cache and is replayed on re-run; I re-fetched with a refresh flag in a scratch wrapper and did not change the repo file. The Stanford copyright-renewal site returned an F5 bot-challenge page instead of robots.txt; not circumvented, so the renewal status of Storrick (558) is unchecked.

summary: Batch 7 (0-based; the queue file labels it batch 8; entries 569, 570, 574, 576, 637, 638, 559, 571, 577, 578, 639, 641) reviewed with real fetches. Verdicts: 11 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY and 1 REJECT (576). No entry is approved for the verbatim quote corpus. 576 is the main finding: its link is a single volume (Ser. I vol. 26 pt. 2, Louisiana/Texas/Gulf operations, GPO 1889), not the full OR set and not Gettysburg. Other findings: 559 names Sallie Myers, not Sallie Broadhead, and links to no primary texts; 577 and 578 are the source of the list's OR page ranges (including its wrong first pages for reports 10 and 134) and their site terms forbid software crawling; 571 overstates Gettysburg content (about 6 of 60 items). Not verified: the text of the two Cupola PDFs (569, 570), which sit behind a Cloudflare challenge that I did not circumvent and which I did not download from the Wayback Machine; the UNT Portal rights panel (574, read from the earlier probe's cached, truncated copy); HathiTrust and eHistory targets (never fetched).
systemic_findings: Entry 576 shows that a 'volume' link can point at the wrong volume: archive.org/details/warofrebellion012602rootrich is Ser. I vol. 26 pt. 2 (Gulf/Louisiana/Texas), not the OR set and not vol. 27. The other 'volume' entries should be checked against the Internet Archive metadata field volume (e.g. v.27:1 for warofrebellion271unit).

Civil War Cycling (entries 577, 578) is the source of the list's OR report numbers, page ranges and HathiTrust links, and the list inherited its errors: first pages of reports 10 (155 vs OCR 168) and 134 (488 vs 486), and a printed typo 74-476 for report 471. The index's HathiTrust seq is itself a near-constant offset (+20 for 371 of 377 Part 1 links, +2 for 205 of 210 Part 2 links), so the QC-REPORT point that the offsets look computed is partly inherited from the index. The list matches the index for 532 of 541 comparable links; in the 9 that differ (reports 102, 131, 251, 298, 330, 385, 392, 407, 448) the index's own offset breaks the constant and the list uses the constant. A human should open those nine on HathiTrust.

The list's Part I has 332 reports where the index has 378: Nos. 327-329, 332-347, 350-358, 360 and 362-378 (artillery, cavalry and Department of Washington reports, OR 27,1 pp. 893-1040) are absent (46 numbers).

civilwarcycling.com's terms forbid software crawling and copying of the site, although robots.txt allows it. Only two index pages and the terms page were fetched here; any further use should be link-out and the OCR index, not re-scraping.

items.written: collection page undated; diaries 1863 (Samuel 30 June to 6 July 1863; Rachel June and July 1863)
items.rights_basis: Page footer carries a link to Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0. The site's copyright statement (fetched) says the site is free for non-commercial research, teaching and private study, and that some material may still be under copyright. The site's Sources page lists The Cormany Diaries (James C. Mohr, ed., University of Pittsburgh Press, 1982) for the Rachel Cormany diary, so the web text may derive from a modern edited edition. Whether the non-commercial term fits this project is an owner decision.
items.evidence: Fetched https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/war/letters-and-diaries/franklin/cormany (HTTP 200, 157,089 bytes; sha256 e6b140fd..., identical to the earlier probe; the host has no robots.txt, 404). Heading Samuel and Rachel Cormany (1863); background says Samuel enlisted as a second lieutenant in the 16th Pennsylvania Cavalry in September 1862; one excerpt is Samuel's service during the Gettysburg Campaign, another is Rachel's account of Chambersburg. The diary pages are FD1007 (Samuel) and FD1006 (Rachel, entry 640); FD1007 fetched (200, 186,817 bytes): Diary of Samuel Cormany (1863) with dated entries 30 June to 6 July 1863 and footnotes. Description check: it says Samuel's diary covers the 16th Pennsylvania Cavalry during the Gettysburg Campaign, and the entries describe the 2 and 3 July fighting (the cavalry brigade, shelling, 'cannonading' on the 3rd) and the battlefield on 5 July. Valley's own About page says each document was proofread by two people against the manuscript; whether the text was written day by day or compiled later is not stated.
items.extraction_notes: Collection index only. Treat each diary (FD1006, FD1007) as its own entry needing a rights decision (CC BY-NC and the possible 1982 edition). The pages are a Nuxt single-page app, so the entry text sits in the server payload; use the FD pages, not the collection page, if the diaries are ever approved.
issues: Rights unresolved: CC BY-NC 4.0 plus a possible 1982 University of Pittsburgh Press edition behind the transcription.
The collection page itself does not contain the diary text; the diaries are separate pages (FD1006, FD1007).
The page title is Letters of the Cormany Family, while the entry calls it a diaries collection page.

summary: Batch 3 (0-based; queue field "batch": 4), 12 entries, all fetched and read. Verdicts: APPROVE 5 (628 Hoke, 633 Christian letter, 645 Hiester, 646 Pollock, 648 Franklin Repository), APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY 6 (630, 631 Leach, 632 Creigh, 640 Cormany, 642 Stouffer, 644 Heyser), REJECT 1 (647 Bitner), NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW 0. Main findings: (1) 630 is a two-page excerpt (book pp. 157-158) of 631, not an independent source. (2) The listed UVM link for 631 now serves only a DSpace app shell with HTTP 200 (the QC probe classed it live); the work is at a new address that I fetched. (3) 632 is a 1940 paper quoting the Creigh diary, not the diary itself. (4) The Valley of the Shadow TEI headers (api.valley.newamericanhistory.org, robots allows all) state the print source and permission for each item, and show that 640, 642 and 644 are transcriptions of in-copyright editions (1982, 1992, 1978). (5) None of the 22 Bitner letters (647) is dated after 25 May 1863. (6) 628 and 633 have public-domain Internet Archive scans, and I confirmed the cited incident and letter text there. Fetches used the repo PoliteClient (honest User-Agent, 1 req/s/host, robots honoured, Perseus not fetched, no browser). archive.org returned HTTP 429 once and refused a connection once, so I backed off. Search-engine summaries (WebSearch) were used only as pointers, and each point that matters was confirmed by a direct fetch, except the Freedley rank and unit (single search summary).
systemic_findings: UVM ScholarWorks moved from bepress to DSpace (page dated 2026-06-16). Old viewcontent.cgi links now return HTTP 200 with a 827-byte Angular shell titled DSpace and no document, and the QC link probe classed 631 as live. Old item addresses (scholarworks.uvm.edu/crvocc/21) still resolve by two 301s to /items/<uuid> and the PDF is at /bitstreams/<uuid>/download. Other scholarworks.uvm.edu links in the list should be re-checked with a body check (title DSpace and under 1 KB means dead).

The Valley of the Shadow (valley.newamericanhistory.org) states provenance and permission per item in a TEI header at api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/papers/<id>.xml (robots allows all): source copy, edition, copyright holder, and 'used with permission' line. For Part XI this shows 640 (Mohr, 1982), 642 (Piston, 1992, Kent State UP) and 644 (Kittochtinny Papers, 1978) are transcriptions of in-copyright editions, while 645-647 are manuscript letters at Duke, UNC and UVA. The site footer has a CC BY-NC 4.0 badge and a Copyright and Fair Use page limiting use to non-commercial; the TEI should be the extraction source (HTML repeats Original and Modern Spelling and, for 644, duplicates two entries).

630 is pp. 157-158 of 631 (identical text, same compiler brackets and footnote); count it as one source. The QC report's claim that all 13 Dickinson Archives links are dead does not hold for housedivided.dickinson.edu/sites/blogdivided/files (this PDF works after a 301 to https).
The probe's byte cap truncated pages at 327,680 bytes (644 is 533 KB, 648 is 397 KB, 630 is 1.7 MB), so truncated probe fetches should not be used as complete evidence.

tools/sources-qc/lib/http.mjs caches a failed robots.txt fetch (status 0, for example ECONNREFUSED after archive.org throttling) and then refuses every later URL on that host as robots_unreadable; I deleted my own cache entry and retried. archive.org answered 429 once during my run, probably because other workflows share the IP.

For Perseus-class entries (633) the Rebellion Record is on the Internet Archive in several copies; BookReader image numbers and page_numbers.json leaf numbers differ (by 31 here), so reviewers must cite printed pages and read the image rather than trusting leaf numbers or the OCR date.

Rights recommendation for unpublished manuscript letters transcribed online after 1977 (645-647 and similar): 17 U.S.C. 303(a) may keep them protected to 2047 if a pre-2003 posting counts as publication, which is why they are tiered A2 and not A1; this is a question for counsel, not a finding.

items.written: 1884 (serialized in the Chambersburg Public Opinion from 12 Jan 1884; describes events of 1861-1864 including the June 1863 occupation)
items.rights_basis: US imprint before 1931. Title page of the Library of Congress scan on the Internet Archive (reminiscencesofw00hoke, fetched) reads Historical Reminiscences of the War ... by J. Hoke, Chambersburg, M. A. Foltz, 1884; archive metadata date 1884, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. The Google Books record is only a second host of the same 1884 book.
items.evidence: Listed link: the QC probe's cached fetch (2026-10-01 03:15Z, which I re-read) of the bare Google Books ?id=8F_WAAAAMAAJ page returned HTTP 200, 'Historical Reminiscences of the War; Or, Incidents which Transpired in and ...', Jacob Hoke, M.A. Foltz, 1884, 211 pages, with preview and free EPUB/PDF buttons. The pg=PA38 anchor was NOT fetched (robots.txt disallows the dq=/pg= parameters). I then fetched IA item reminiscencesofw00hoke (metadata API, 1.3 MB djvu.txt, page_numbers.json, hOCR page index). Its title page matches the entry (title, author J. Hoke, Foltz, 1884) and a front note says the chapters appeared weekly in Public Opinion from 12 Jan 1884. Description check 1: in the chapter on Jenkins's occupation (mid-June 1863) Hoke writes that soldiers hunted Black residents, free and enslaved, and sent some south under guard; a well-known Black resident, Esquire Hall, was carried off behind a rebel horseman, Hoke fetched the Rev. Dr. B. S. Schneck, who went to Jenkins's headquarters and vouched that Hall was a long-time resident and not a fugitive, and Hall was released; Schneck said a Jenkins staff officer who had once heard him preach in Virginia helped. That is a captured Black resident freed through a Confederate connection, as the entry says. Check 2: the same passage has Jenkins telling Schneck he would not burn a hay stack because Lee's whole army was coming. Page check: counting lines between the OCR page numbers and the hOCR page index both put the Hall passage on leaf 44, which page_numbers.json labels printed page 38, matching the Google Books anchor PA38.
items.extraction_notes: Use the IA scan (adapter archive-fulltext), not Google Books. djvu.txt is OCR with hard-wrapped, hyphenated lines (for example a word broken across lines), double spaces, two-column order, and page-number lines partly lost or misread (p. 34 read as 54, p. 35 as 15, pp. 36-40 absent), so take page cites from the hOCR page index plus _page_numbers.json, not from the text. A second scan exists (reminiscences00hoke, Gettysburg College). Hoke later expanded this material into The Great Invasion of 1863 (Dayton, 1887; a different edition, do not merge). Segment by chapter heading; the Black-resident anecdotes sit inside the Jenkins chapter.
issues: Google Books page anchor PA38 unchecked on that host; the IA scan confirms the passage is on printed p. 38.
IA catalog title drops the word Historical; the title page has it.
Retrospective (21 years later) and a Union civilian's voice; Hoke saw the Hall incident himself but the Schneck-Jenkins exchange is secondhand.
Google Books page lists an introduction by A. K. McClure; I did not reconcile that with the unsigned introduction in the LoC scan.

items.written: 1863-07-13 (the PDF also holds letters of 1863-07-15 and 1863-07-18, plus the end of an earlier letter)
items.rights_basis: The PDF is a two-page photocopy (printed pages 157-158) of the 2002 UVM Center for Research on Vermont edition (entry 631), whose copyright page reads (c) 2002 University of Vermont, all rights reserved; the repository page for that edition shows CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The Dickinson PDF carries no licence statement. Leach's own words are 1863, but this text is reachable only through the 2002 edition, with the compiler's bracketed headers and footnote.
items.evidence: I fetched the listed http URL: 301 to https, then HTTP 200 application/pdf, 1,699,763 bytes (the earlier probe was truncated at 327,680), 2 pages, created 2018-06-20 with Mac OS X Quartz PDFContext, scanned images with a text layer, page footers 157 and 158. Content: Leach writes to his wife from near Funkstown, Md. (July 13), Boonsboro (July 15) and Berlin, Md. (July 18); says his brigade skirmished toward Funkstown, that the 3rd Brigade of his division rejoined after leaving Gettysburg, that a man he looked for in the 1st Corps was taken prisoner at Gettysburg, and describes a mutilated Black boy left in a barn. Description check 1 (Union soldier in the pursuit after Gettysburg): the letters are dated 10-18 July 1863, his unit is Co. H, 2nd Vermont. Check 2: the sections quote the pursuit and the Potomac crossing. Identity: the text of both pages is identical to the text I extracted from the UVM edition PDF (leaves 173-174, printed 157-158), including the bracketed header [After the battle of Funkstown] and a footnote citing Marshall, A War of the People (UPNE 1999) for the New York draft riots. So 630 is an excerpt of 631. The QC report's 13 dead Dickinson Archives links do not apply to this housedivided.dickinson.edu URL, which works.
items.extraction_notes: Do not ingest as its own source; ingest (if ever) from 631 with page cites. Text layer is OCR (for example 'bailie' for battle, 'ki lled'), so check against the page images. Brackets and the footnote are the compiler's, not Leach's.
issues: Duplicate of 631 (pp. 157-158); do not count as an independent source.
Entry says letter, singular and July 1863; the PDF contains three dated letters plus the tail of another.
Single mention of the Gettysburg battle; this is pursuit-phase context, not fighting.

items.written: Letters 1861-06-09 to 1864-06-26 (237 per the Introduction; the Foreword says 247); edition 2002
items.rights_basis: Copyright page of the PDF: (c) 2002 The University of Vermont, All rights reserved, ISBN 0-944277-38-1. The live repository item page (fetched) shows License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/). 'Open access' therefore means free to read; NonCommercial/NoDerivatives bars ingestion as an adapted corpus.
items.evidence: The listed viewcontent.cgi URL (QC probe cache, which I re-read) returns HTTP 200 but only an 827-byte DSpace Angular shell titled DSpace, with no PDF: UVM ScholarWorks moved from bepress to DSpace (page last-modified 2026-06-16), so the old link is dead in disguise (I cannot render it, no browser allowed). Wayback availability API gives a 2024-07-09 capture; I fetched it (26,194,004 bytes, 261 pages, PDF title ''Dear Wife'': the Civil War letters of Chester K. Leach). The old item address scholarworks.uvm.edu/crvocc/21 (printed in the PDF's citation line) now answers 301, 301, then HTTP 200 at https://scholarworks.uvm.edu/items/9df80ca3-4c1b-4e03-9b9e-b2e3e1f31c13 (server-rendered metadata: 2002, Center for Research on Vermont Occasional Papers, authors Leach, Anna A. Montague Leach, Feidner, Hand, Gallagher, Marshall). A HEAD request on its download bitstream returned 200 application/pdf (file crvoccpaper20small.pdf; I did not download that file). Title page: Occasional Paper #20, compiled by Edward J. Feidner, UVM, 2002. Description check 1 (complete edited edition): the introduction says 237 letters from 9 June 1861 to 26 June 1864 to his wife Ann, chronological, with a Who's Who. Check 2: the letter of 9 July 1863 says Leach's corps marched to the field by the 2nd, his brigade held the extreme left on 3 July and was not engaged, and he describes the cannonade of the 3rd and the pursuit via Emmitsburg; letters of 18 and 20 June, an undated June letter from near Manchester, and 13, 15 and 18 July cover the march and pursuit.
items.extraction_notes: If ever ingested, use the PDF (text layer with OCR slips); printed page = PDF page minus 15. Letters headed Dear Wife; bracketed headers and footnotes are the compiler's. Compiler statement: Leach copied most letters into a postwar copybook, so wording may be postwar. Campaign letters are on printed pp. 150-158.
issues: Listed URL no longer serves the document; use the items page or crvocc/21 redirect.
Foreword (247 letters) and Introduction (237) disagree.
Letters were partly postwar-transcribed by Leach himself.
630 is a 2-page excerpt of this book.

items.written: Paper read 1940-02-29; quotes diary entries of 1862-08-01 to 1865-07-20 (June 1863 entries by Rev. Thomas Creigh)
items.rights_basis: The page is a 1940 paper by the Rev. J. D. Edmiston Turner (Papers Read Before the Kittochtinny Historical Society, 29 Feb 1940) with Creigh's 1860s diary quoted inside it. A US work of 1927-1963 is protected only if renewed; renewal was not checked, and the Internet Archive holds only the society's pre-1931 volumes (1898-1908), so no public-domain copy was found. The quoted 1863 diary words are old, but the selection and narration are Turner's. The Wayback host adds no licence.
items.evidence: The Wayback capture (2008-12-01) answered HTTP 200 (35,503 bytes; cached probe fetch which I re-read). Its title block reads Civil War Days in Mercersburg as Related in the Diary of the Rev. Thomas Creigh, D.D., August 1, 1862 to July 20, 1865, prepared by the Rev. J. D. Edmiston Turner, Papers Read Before the Kittochtinny Historical Society, February 29, 1940. The text is Turner's narrative with the diary entries inside quotation marks, not the diary. Description check 1: the entry of Friday 26 June 1863 is quoted in full there (guerrillas passing with local Black residents, among them two named men, to be sold into slavery; a threat to burn houses sheltering contrabands or firearms). Check 2: further passages cover the raid of 24 June, Imboden's requisition on 30 June, the 1 July raid that took six or seven free Black people, and the 5-8 July events (wounded and prisoners, news of Gettysburg). Creigh is correctly described as Mercersburg's Presbyterian pastor (installed 1831, died 1880). The new Valley site's Franklin letters-and-diaries index lists no Creigh page.
items.extraction_notes: Wayback page has a leftover server-side-include error line at the top; plain HTML text, easy to segment by paragraph, but quoted diary text and Turner's prose are interleaved, so any extraction must separate the quoted passages. OCR-like typos remain (for example 'servevd', 'negroes' spelling is original). Cite as Turner 1940, not as the diary.
issues: Entry calls it the diary; it is a 1940 paper quoting the diary, so title and kind need correcting (secondary compilation with primary excerpts).
Rights status of the 1940 paper unknown.
Only a Wayback copy of the old UVA page exists in what I found; the new Valley site lacks it.
Valley's primary-source list names the same item (Kittochtinny Historical Society Papers), which I confirmed.

items.rights_basis: Frank Moore, ed., The Rebellion Record, Seventh Volume, New York: D. Van Nostrand, 1864 (title page read in the OCR of IA item rebellionrecordd07moor; archive metadata possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT). US imprint before 1931; the letter itself is from 1863.
items.evidence: The Perseus link was NOT fetched: the QC probe recorded its robots.txt as Disallow: / for this host, and I honoured that. I found the same book on the Internet Archive: item rebellionrecordd07moor (868 images, New York Public Library copy; a University of California copy rebellrecord07moorrich also exists; my fetch of its text failed, so unread). I fetched its djvu.txt (5.4 MB), the page-number JSON and the OCR page index, and read the page image. The contents list gives A Rebel Letter at p. 325; page image (BookReader n434) shows Documents p. 325 with the heading A REBEL LETTER, the note that it was picked up on the battlefield of Gettysburg by a member of a Philadelphia regiment, the dateline Camp near Greenwood, Pa., June 28, 1863, addressed to his wife, and signed Wm. S. Christian. The OCR misreads the date as June 2? and the signature, so the image was needed. Description check: the writer says he was offered his choice among captured Black people and refused, in the words 'We took a lot of negroes yesterday' (Christian, 28 June 1863, p. 325); he then turned them loose, which the entry does not mention. Identity: Encyclopedia Virginia (fetched) says William S. Christian was promoted colonel of the 55th Virginia on 23 June 1863 and wrote a letter dated 28 June 1863 to his wife that was found on the Gettysburg battlefield.
items.extraction_notes: Use the IA scan (adapter archive-fulltext). Two OCR page numberings differ by 31 in this item (page_numbers.json lists printed p. 325 at leaf 465; the BookReader image n434 shows p. 325), so cite by printed page and check the image. About 900 words; one letter; split by paragraph. The letter is attached under Doc. 82's material and ends before Doc. 83 (Rebel attack near Rockville).
issues: The regiment (55th Virginia) and rank are not in the printed letter; they come from Encyclopedia Virginia, so cite that for identification.
Perseus copy not verified (robots); the IA book is the verified source.
The volume's IA date metadata (1861-1863; 1864-68) is loose; the title page says 1864.
The task text says SHSP; this entry is the Rebellion Record, so the SHSP wording does not apply.

items.rights_basis: The Valley TEI header (api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/papers/FD1006.xml, fetched) names its source copy as Mohr and Winslow, eds., The Cormany Diaries: A Northern Family in the Civil War (University of Pittsburgh Press, 1982), says the footnotes and introduction are the editors' work, and says the text is used with permission from a published source; Valley copyright 1998 Rector and Visitors of the University of Virginia. Valley footer carries a CC BY-NC 4.0 badge and its Copyright and Fair Use page says free for non-commercial research, teaching, scholarship, and private study, and that some materials may still be under copyright. A diary first printed in 1982 may be protected to 2047 under 17 U.S.C. 303(a) (counsel to confirm).
items.evidence: I read the Valley page (HTTP 200, 280 KB, server-rendered; robots.txt 404, so unrestricted) and its TEI. 23 dated entries from 14 June to 6 July 1863 by Rachel Cormany, whose husband Samuel served in the Union army; she lived in Chambersburg. Check 1 (Jenkins's cavalry arriving, capture of Black residents): the 15-16 June entries describe the panic as Milroy's wagons fled and the rebels arrived, with Black women and children, some raised in town, driven off like cattle; the editor's note identifies Gen. Albert G. Jenkins and says official records confirm his arrival time. Check 2 (retreat): the 5 July entry reports citizens capturing wagons of wounded from the late battle and a report that the whole rebel army is retreating; 4 July reports a flag raised and rumours of a dreadful fight. Entries of 2-3 July mention firing and hunger but no battle scene (she reports rumours).
items.extraction_notes: Prefer the TEI XML (entries as dated divisions, footnotes separate) over the HTML, which shows Original and Modern Spelling versions and the editors' footnotes. Exclude the editors' footnotes and introduction (1982 copyright).
issues: Underlying diary text is 1863 but reachable only through a copyrighted 1982 edition via Valley permission.
TEI names the assistant editor Robert E. Winslow III while the Valley sources page says Richard E. Winslow, III.
Home-front observer: no battle narrative.

items.rights_basis: Valley TEI header (FD5500.xml, fetched) names the source copy as William Garrett Piston, ed., The Rebs Are Yet Thick About Us: The Civil War Diary of Amos Stouffer of Chambersburg, Civil War History 38:3 (Sept. 1992) 210-231, reproduced by permission of The Kent State University Press; Valley copyright 2002 UVA; footer CC BY-NC 4.0 badge. Edition published 1992 (diary first printed then), so a rights holder exists.
items.evidence: Valley page HTTP 200 (298 KB, server-rendered): 98 dated entries, 6 Jan to 13 Dec 1863, with ellipses showing it is an excerpted edition. Check 1 (horse seizures): 17 June says the rebels are scouring the country for horses, 16 June says Milroy's 500 wagons and 2,000 horses went through, 2 July says about 1,000 cavalry camped in the family's fields, stole bees and chickens, and took 150 bushels of corn paid in Confederate scrip. Check 2 (rumours of the battle, army's passage): 3 July says rumours of a great battle about Gettysburg; 26-27 June report Lee's army in the valley and A. P. Hill's division marching toward Baltimore; 7-8 July he visits the Gettysburg field and describes the unburied dead, which is aftermath. The page's Biography section is empty, so farmer is supported only by the farm work in the entries, not by a stated biography.
items.extraction_notes: Use the TEI (entries n=date). The page shows Original and Modern Spelling duplicates. The text is Piston's selection, not the whole diary.
issues: Farmer unverified (empty biography).
Excerpted edition under copyright; permission was given to the Valley, not to downstream users.
Includes a July 7-8 battlefield visit, so partly aftermath.

items.written: 1862-09-29 to 1863-10-26 (TEI creation range; the TEI note says Sept 1862 to July 1863)
items.rights_basis: Valley TEI header (FD1004.xml, fetched): source is the William Heyser diary in Papers Read Before the Kittochtinny Historical Society (1971-1978), vol. 14 (Mercersburg Printing, 1978), with W. S. Bowers's parenthetical notes turned into footnotes; project description says used with permission from the Kittochtinny Historical Society; Valley copyright 1998 UVA. A 1978 edition of an 1860s manuscript: protected by the edition and possibly to 2047 under 17 U.S.C. 303(a) (counsel to confirm).
items.evidence: I refetched the page (533 KB; the probe copy was truncated at 327,680 bytes) and the TEI (116 KB). Biography: William Heyser, born 1796, shopkeeper in Chambersburg's South Ward, died 5 Nov 1863; the diary is volume 8 of 8 (four lost). Check 1 (occupation): the entry on 15 June reports rebels entering and demanding surrender, 27 June describes about 35,000 rebels marching past including Lee and Hill, and 29 June onward cover requisitions. Check 2 (aftermath): 4 July reports captures of rebel cavalry and infantry and Carlisle shelled; 5 July reports 12 wagons of Gettysburg wounded left at the hospital and Milroy's cavalry passing. Heyser was 66, so elderly is right.
items.extraction_notes: Use the TEI. The HTML page shows the first entry of March and May 1863 twice at the top (before the Sept 1862 start) and Original/Modern Spelling duplicates; some dates in the print edition are misnumbered and were corrected by the Valley. 179 entries.
issues: Valley date corrections mean the text is not a faithful 1978 transcription.
TEI range and TEI note disagree on the end date.
Edition copyright and permission issue.

items.rights_basis: Six manuscript letters of 1863 from the Rubenstein Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Duke University (TEI source line), used with permission from Duke; Valley transcription copyright 2002 UVA; Valley footer CC BY-NC 4.0. The writers died long ago, but these unpublished letters first became public through the Valley, and 17 U.S.C. 303(a) could protect them to 2047 if that 2002 posting counts as publication; counsel should decide.
items.evidence: The page is a Valley collection index (HTTP 200) whose payload lists letters F1103-F1108; I fetched the six TEI files. Dates: 11, 18, 22 June, 19, 27, 29 July 1863. F1103 is headed Augusta County in the Valley's metadata though filed in the Franklin set. Check 1: the letters of 19 July (from Gettysburg) and 29 July are by H. W. Freedley, who says he was dangerously wounded in the battle of the 2nd, shot in the left knee, and lies at the house of D. Wills Esq. in Gettysburg. A web search summary identifies him as Capt. Henry W. Freedley, 3rd U.S. Infantry, wounded 2 July (single secondary source). Check 2: the letter of 27 July by Joseph Hiester to his wife, written from Gettysburg, says he has been nursing Freedley for two days, describes the wound below the knee, the bed he bought in Philadelphia, and that he stays at the McClellan Hotel. The entry says Hiester travelled to treat him; the letter says nursing, so treat is a small stretch.
items.extraction_notes: Use the six TEI files (api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/papers/F1103..F1108.xml); each page shows Original and Modern Spelling. Exclude Valley summaries. Wills household details (David Wills, host of Lincoln in November) are useful for the town map.
issues: Collection page, not a single document; six letters.
Title metadata anomaly (Augusta County) on F1103.
Freedley's unit and rank rest on a single search summary plus the letters' own headings (3rd U.S. Infantry camp; 2nd Division Regulars, 5th Corps).
Rights need review (CC BY-NC site licence; unpublished-manuscript question).

items.rights_basis: Manuscript at UNC Southern Historical Collection, A. D. Pollock Papers #865 (TEI source line; used with permission from UNC). The UNC finding aid (fetched) says no usage restrictions and that copyright is retained by the authors or descendants as US law stipulates. Pollock died in 1863, so the letter is old, but it was first made public in the Valley's 2002 UVA-copyrighted transcription (footer CC BY-NC 4.0), so the unpublished-manuscript rule in 17 U.S.C. 303(a) needs a human look.
items.evidence: Valley page HTTP 200 and TEI F4045.xml fetched. The letter is dated Headquarters Kemper's Brigade, Chambersburg, 30 June 1863, to his father; the writer says the army crossed the Potomac at Williamsport on the 26th and entered Chambersburg on the 28th. Check 1 (morale, reverence for Lee): he says discipline is far better than the previous year, the soldiers have an almost fanatical confidence in Lee, and he encloses Lee's order. Check 2 (foraging): he says he has heard of no outrage to person or property and that the army lives well on the country, which matches the Valley summary. UNC finding aid: Thomas Gordon Pollock (1838-1863), captain in the Confederate army, killed in the Gettysburg campaign; the finding aid does not say he was on Kemper's staff, so officer is supported but the staff role is not.
items.extraction_notes: One letter (about 6 KB); the web page prints it twice (Original and Modern Spelling), so dedupe. Use the TEI; exclude the Valley summary.
issues: Writer was killed at Gettysburg, so the letter is one of his last; the finding aid gives no day of death.
Rights as above.
Capt. rank from UNC, not stated in the letter.

items.rights_basis: Letters held at the Small Special Collections Library, University of Virginia (TEI project line, used with permission), Valley copyright 1998 UVA, footer CC BY-NC 4.0; unpublished manuscripts first posted by the Valley, same 303(a) question as 645; moot because of the relevance finding.
items.evidence: Collection page HTTP 200 (158 KB). Its payload lists 22 letters F0700-F0721, which I fetched as TEI (about 60,000 characters). Authors: Alex Cressler 6 (Chambersburg, May-July 1861), D. F. Daihl 1 (Murfreesboro, May 1863), Thad Donely 4 (early 1863), William Kindig 2 and William Martin 1 (1862), D. R. P. Shoemaker 8 (Ohio unit, Tennessee, 1862-63). The latest letter is dated 25 May 1863, before the campaign. A keyword search of all 22 for Gettysburg, invasion, Lee or Hooker found only a 1862 report of rebels retreating and the 1861 word invasion used jokingly. So the entry's count (22) is right but it is wrong that all are from Pennsylvania regiments serving (Cressler was a civilian teacher; Shoemaker served in Ohio) and no letter touches the invasion or battle.
items.extraction_notes: If a human wants pre-campaign context, use the TEI files; for this project there is nothing in the campaign window.
issues: No letter falls in the campaign or battle window.
Description overstates: includes six civilian letters and eight letters from an Ohio soldier.
Two items carry date oddities (F0707 text says Jan 5 1862 while the title says 1863).

items.rights_basis: Weekly newspaper published 8 July 1863: I read the masthead on the Valley's scan (Vol. 70, Chambersburg, Wednesday, July 8, 1863, No. 24). A US imprint before 1931, so the printed text is public domain. A2 rather than A1 because the quotable text comes from the Valley's 1998 transcription (UVA staff, footer CC BY-NC 4.0 and a statement permitting non-commercial use only), and the page carries Valley-written summaries and descriptions that must not be copied.
items.evidence: Page HTTP 200, 397 KB (the probe copy was truncated at 327,680 bytes); eight pages, TEI (pa.fr.fr.1863.07.08.xml, 146 KB) and an eight-page scan PDF (4.1 MB, 3744 x 5184 px per page, image only) fetched. summary: Batch 1 (queue batch 2; 12 entries: 653-656, 544, 552, 579, 598, 600, 601, 602, 604) verified with real fetches. Verdicts: 9 APPROVE (653, 654, 655, 656, 544, 552, 598, 602, 604), 1 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (600, with a corrected URL), 1 NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW (579), 1 REJECT (601). Main findings: (1) the three New York Final Report entries are Vol. I twice (653, 654) and Vol. III (655), never "Vols. I & II" or "the set", and Vol. II is in none of them. (2) 544 and 552 are real and verified in Internet Archive scans of SHSP vols. 7 (1879) and 37 (1909), so the Perseus links are not needed, but both descriptions are partly wrong (544 was the first full printing, not a reprint; 552's two articles attack rather than defend Stuart's conduct). (3) 601 is not an eyewitness account: it is a one-paragraph family anecdote in a 1937 Wyoming typescript by a woman born at Carlisle on 6 Jan 1864, six months after the shelling. (4) 600's listed URL has a typo and returns a generic listing page with HTTP 200; the corrected slug returns the article abstract. (5) 598, 604 and 602 are all Carlisle shelling accounts (Garnett for Stuart; Patterson and Leland in Landis' Philadelphia battery), verified page-by-page against Internet Archive scans of pre-1931 books, with printed pages matching the Google Books anchors. (6) Compliance disclosure: I made two requests to hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu seconds apart before reading its robots.txt (Crawl-delay: 600); no further requests went to that host. Working copies of fetched material are in the scratchpad folder sv2b1 and the PoliteClient cache under C:/Users/mlege/gettysburg-map/tmp/sources-v2/cache/http; nothing in the repo outside that cache was written.
systemic_findings: Compliance disclosure: hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu (the current House Divided archive) publishes Crawl-delay: 600 in robots.txt. I fetched its robots.txt and then two pages (/node/40274 and /node/40265) in separate process runs within about a minute, before I had read the Crawl-delay line. That breaches the 600-second delay. I made no further requests to that host and used only those two pages (Garnett and Patterson transcriptions, used as cross-checks, not as text sources). The cause is a gap in the shared client: tools/sources-qc/lib/http.mjs PoliteClient.waitSlot applies Crawl-delay only relative to the same process's previous request, so the first request of every new run is never delayed. A fix would store per-host last-request timestamps on disk and apply the host's Crawl-delay to the first request after reading robots.txt. Other hosts: archive.org (many requests, at least 1.5 s apart per process, many served through dn*.archive.org download hosts), gardnerlibrary.org (Crawl-delay: 10; one network request, about 40 minutes after the probe's), housedivided.dickinson.edu (robots.txt 404: no restrictions; 2 requests). books.google.com listed URLs with dq=/pg= were never fetched. One googleapis.com Books API call returned HTTP 429 and was not retried. Parallel batch verifiers share archive.org and each throttles only itself, so the aggregate rate could exceed 1 request/second/host.

Perseus replacement: the SHSP articles in Part IV can be verified and extracted from Internet Archive scans, and for these two I did so. Vol. 7 (1879) is southernhistoric7187sout (610 images; also southernhistoric0007sout, 618) and Vol. 37 (1909) is southernhistoric3719sout. Vol. 7 is not in the plan's SRC-08 volume list and holds Stuart's full report (pp. 401-434); the registry should add it. Page maps there are good (confidence 100 and 98).

The New York Final Report set is three volumes, paged continuously (I about 1-454 and onward, II about 455-934, III 935-1461). Entries 653 and 654 are two different scans of Vol. I (1900) and 655 is Vol. III (1902); no entry covers Vol. II. The IA item title 'NEW YORK AT GETTYSBURG Vol I & II' on item 653 is wrong for its content (Vol. I only, 540 images) and is probably where the entry's 'Vols. I & II' came from. The plan's SRC-03 primary (finalreportongettys01burgrich, 548 images) is a third Vol. I scan. Ingest each volume once.

Descriptions in the list are template-like and wrong in specifics: 653 (Fox's narrative covers the whole battle, not each unit; 33 unit sketches are the editor's), 654 and 655 (one volume, not the set or 'the same work' at the same date), 544 ('reprinted' when it was the first full printing), 552 (the Talcott review is critical of Stuart; the Times-Dispatch note does not attach to these two papers), 601 (author not an eyewitness). Reviewer rule: check the specific claim, not just the title.

Soft 404: entry 600's URL has a slug typo and returns HTTP 200 with a generic page ('CCHS Publications Browsing'). The link probe classified it only as 'redirected', which hides the failure; a check that compares the page title with the entry title would catch this class (the probe already does this for 'redirected_to_generic_page' on other hosts).

Google Books page anchors (pg=) cannot be checked by a compliant bot. For public-domain books the anchor can instead be confirmed from the Internet Archive scan's running heads (done for 598, 602, 604); for modern copyrighted editions (579) it cannot, and such entries need a human to open the page.

Carlisle shelling cluster (598, 602, 604, and previously rejected 595): all are about 1 July 1863 and all but 598 are Union gunners or townspeople in Landis' Philadelphia battery under Gen. W. F. Smith; Leland names Patterson in the same chapter, and Garnett's letter quotes Stuart's report (OR 27 pt. 2 p. 696) and Smith's. For historian use these items corroborate each other and the OR27 reports already ingested; they should be tagged as retrospective (1892-1896 letters, 1893 memoir) and carry the OR reports as the primary.

IA page_numbers.json coverage differs by item: 653 has 427 of 538 leaves labelled, 654 only 295 of 545 (confidence 64), 655 441 of 636, 656 479 of 660, SHSP vol. 7 590 of 608, vol. 37 373 of 396; the Wingate scan (historyoftwenty00wing) and the Cornell Leland scan have none. Any citation to a printed page from these needs the running-head check described in each item's extraction notes.

Rights note for the registry: Google's front matter on the 654 scan asks for non-commercial use and no automated querying; that is a request tied to Google's scan, not to the 1900 text, but legal review may want to prefer the plan's primary Internet Archive scan for ingestion.

items.written: Letter dated Norfolk, Va., 31 May 1892, to Gen. George W. Wingate; printed in Wingate's 1896 regimental history, pp. 221-225. Retrospective by 29 years.
items.rights_basis: Wingate, History of the Twenty-second Regiment of the National Guard of the State of New York, New York: E. W. Dayton, 1896. The scan's front matter reads 'COPYRIGHT, 1896 GENERAL GEORGE W. WINGATE'; archive.org metadata (item historyoftwenty00wing) date 1896, publisher New York, E. W. Dayton; Google Books page for CJQQAAAAYAAJ shows 'E. W. Dayton, 1896', full view. Pre-1931 publication, so public domain, including the letter first printed there.
items.evidence: Exact Google Books URL (dq=, pg=PA221) not fetched (robots.txt); the cached bare page https://books.google.com/books?id=CJQQAAAAYAAJ (HTTP 200) names the book and 'E. W. Dayton, 1896 ... 762 pages', full view. Read the Internet Archive copy historyoftwenty00wing (metadata and djvu.txt 752,583 bytes; item page HTTP 200). On the page whose running head reads 'History of the Twenty-second Regiment 221', Wingate introduces 'the following letter from Col. T. S. Garnet, aid to Gen. Stuart', followed by 'Norfolk, Va., May 31, 1892. Gen. George W. Wingate ... I proceed to give you an account of the advance upon Carlisle ... made by General J. E. B. Stuart ... on the evening of July 1, 1863'. So p. 221 is the first page of the account, matching the PA221 anchor. Claim 1 (staff officer, shelling of Carlisle): the letter says Fitz Lee's brigade alone invested Carlisle, that Stuart sent a flag of truce demanding surrender, and that the artillery opened fire after dark. Claim 2 (quoted in the regimental history): it is a letter reprinted in the history. A modern House Divided transcription (hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu/node/40274, transcriber John Osborne 2013) independently cites 'Wingate ... (New York: Edwin W. Dayton, 1896), 221-225' and carries the same text, including Garnett's note that a word from Early to Stuart 'would have saved us the long march to Carlisle and back to Gettysburg'.
items.extraction_notes: Adapter: archive-fulltext on historyoftwenty00wing (ABBYY 8.0, noisy: running heads garbled, e.g. 'W^iBior^ of t0e ...', numerals read '1S92'). Wingate spells the name 'Garnet' and gives him the rank 'Col.'. The House Divided page is a modern transcription (cross-check only).
