items.written: Article in Cumberland County History, 2013, Vol. 30 (author Rachael Zuch); it quotes 1863 newspapers and an 1882 Fitzhugh Lee letter. Secondary, about 150 years after the events.
items.rights_basis: Page footer: 'Copyright (c) 2014-2026 Cumberland County Historical Society All rights reserved.' No open license. The full article is a page of the whole journal volume PDF (gardnerlibrary.org/sites/default/files/vol30n1.pdf#page=79), not fetched.
items.evidence: The listed URL (slug 'ftizhugh', a typo) answers 301 http to https, then HTTP 200 with the generic page title 'CCHS Publications Browsing' (an index of journal issues and articles), so it is a soft 404 and does not show the article. The corrected slug https://gardnerlibrary.org/journal/fitzhugh-lee-reconciling-north-and-south-carlisle-pa (fetched once, HTTP 200; the site's robots.txt allows it with Crawl-delay: 10, which I respected) shows the title 'Fitzhugh Lee: Reconciling North and South in Carlisle, PA', journal issue 2013 Volume 30, author Zuch, Rachael, and an abstract. Claim 1, Lee's role at Carlisle: the abstract says Stuart directed Fitzhugh Lee to attack the town on 1 July after Gen. William F. Smith refused to surrender. That matches Garnett's letter (entry 598) and Stuart's report quoted there, which say Fitz Lee's brigade invested the place; the abstract overstates Lee as the 'leader in charge', since Stuart commanded. Claim 2, later reconciliation: the abstract describes his return to Carlisle 33 years after the shelling and quotes an 1882 letter in which he says he proceeded against Carlisle with much regret. The full article was not read, only the abstract and metadata.
items.extraction_notes: Link-out only. If a primary is wanted, the article's quoted items (1863 Carlisle Herald and American pieces; Lee's 1882 letter) would have to be sourced from their originals, not from this article.
issues: Listed URL has a typo ('ftizhugh') and serves a generic listing page with HTTP 200 (soft 404).
Article is mostly about postwar reconciliation; the shelling is background.
Full text not read (abstract only).
Overstates Fitz Lee as the commander at Carlisle.

items.written: Typescript signed 14 June 1937 (74 years after the events), Wyoming State Archives; the author was born at Carlisle on 6 Jan 1864.
items.rights_basis: A three-page scan of a 1937 typescript headed 'Wyoming State Archives' and hosted on the House Divided blog (path /files/2018/06/); no copyright notice, license or repository rights statement on any page. The text is unpublished as far as the PDF shows, and the author's death date is unknown, so its status cannot be established from the file.
items.evidence: Fetched http://housedivided.dickinson.edu/sites/blogdivided/files/2018/06/Anna-Fosdick-recollection.pdf (301 to https; HTTP 200; application/pdf; full file 1,080,976 bytes, re-fetched because the earlier probe was truncated). It has 3 pages that are images only, so I rendered and read them. Page 1: a foreword, 'The incidents related in this article, THE ARGESHEIMER FAMILY, are given from my own knowledge', signed Mrs. Anna M. M. Fosdick, 14 June 1937. Page 2: 'The Argesheimer Family by Mrs. Anna (Argesheimer) Fosdick' covering her father John Henry Argesheimer, a German-born army bandmaster, and her mother Harriet Lavenia Wallace (born 1837 at Gettysburg); the only Carlisle shelling content is a short passage in which she says she remembers hearing her mother describe wounded exchanged Union prisoners being fed in the Carlisle market when Rebel shells began bursting over it. Page 3: the children listed with 'Anna Mary Magdalene (Mrs. C. H. Fosdick, Carey Block, Cheyenne), born at Carlisle, Pennsylvania, January 6, 1864', that is six months after the shelling of 1 July 1863, then the family's move to Fort D. A. Russell, Wyoming in 1875. So the author was not an eyewitness: the description 'Carlisle woman's recollection of the shelling' is false; this is secondhand family tradition from her mother, recorded in 1937 in a family history, in a few sentences. I did not identify the Dickinson blog post that hosts the PDF.
items.extraction_notes: Do not ingest as a recollection of the shelling. If kept at all, it is a one-paragraph family anecdote (mother's account, relayed in 1937) usable only as a link-out example of local memory, after a rights check with Wyoming State Archives. The PDF is images only and would need manual transcription.
issues: Description is wrong: the author was born after the event and relays her mother's story.
Typescript from Wyoming State Archives, not a Carlisle source; unknown rights and provenance (a 1937 unpublished item).
Content is a few sentences inside an unrelated family history.
Image-only PDF.

items.written: Events June-July 1863; printed in Memoirs, New York: D. Appleton, 1893 (the preface says it was written with no intention to publish; composition date unknown); the metadata notes it closes with 1870. Retrospective by about 30 years.
items.rights_basis: Title page in the Cornell scan (archive.org cu31924022024081): 'MEMOIRS BY CHARLES GODFREY LELAND (HANS BREITMANN), NEW YORK, D. APPLETON AND COMPANY, 1893', 'COPYRIGHT, 1893, by D. Appleton and Company'; metadata date 1893; Cornell's notice in the scan: no known copyright restrictions in the United States on the use of the text. Pre-1931 imprint. The Gale 1968 reprint (memoirs0000lela) and the London Heinemann editions are different editions and must not be used.
items.evidence: The listed Google URL (dq=, pg=PA254) was not fetched (robots.txt); the cached bare page https://books.google.com/books?id=O7Ud9eFYGWcC (HTTP 200) shows 'Memoirs, Charles Godfrey Leland, D. Appleton, 1893, 439 pages', full view. Read the Internet Archive Cornell scan cu31924022024081 (item page HTTP 200; metadata; djvu.txt 942,091 bytes). Chapter V, 'Life during the Civil War and its sequence, 1862-1866' (opens p. 245), has a summary that reads, in part, 'The Emergency - I enter an artillery company ... I see rebel scouts near Harrisburg - The shelling of Carlisle ... Stewart Patterson ... The battle of Gettysburg - The retreat of Lee'. Running head '254 MEMOIRS.' marks the page: it is mid-account of the Carlisle shelling of 1 July 1863, with his captain Landis saying shells would not hurt 'till they hit you' and a shell-burst by a lamp-post, and p. 255 continues the anecdote about Theodore Fassitt's horse. So the PA254 anchor lands on a real Carlisle passage. Claim 1: militia volunteer in the emergency campaign (artillery company under Gen. W. F. Smith, Landis' battery). Claim 2: Gettysburg relevance is campaign only: Leland writes that, as raw recruits, they were 'not put under fire at Gettysburg, but kept in Smith's reserve' (p. 262), and he describes campfires seen the night before the battle. His account of Carlisle is a union-side counterpart to entries 598 and 604; Patterson, named in his chapter summary, served in the same battery.
items.extraction_notes: Adapter: archive-fulltext on cu31924022024081 (ABBYY 8.0). The item's page_numbers.json is only a stub, so take printed pages from the running heads ('NNN MEMOIRS.' / 'LIFE DURING THE CIVIL WAR. NNN'); relevant range pp. 245-270 (leaves roughly 258-285; chapter-wide search not exhaustive). The chapter also contains footnoted letters from a comrade (apparently R. W. Gilder, to be confirmed against the print) and a ballad-related aside: tag quoted letters as separate voices. Five other 1893 Appleton scans exist on IA (memoirs00lelagoog, memoirs01lelagoog, memoirs02lelagoog, memoirs00lela, memoirsx00lelaiala); pick one.
issues: Page anchor not fetchable on Google Books for bots; verified through the Cornell scan's running heads (Appleton edition only: the Heinemann London edition has different pagination).
Retrospective, anecdotal prose with humour and hearsay; frames events as personal adventure.
Not at the battle itself (kept in reserve).

items.written: Undated letter from C. Stuart Patterson to Gen. George W. Wingate, written after 1864 (it refers to having read Wingate's 'admirable description' of the march) and before the 1896 history, pp. 214-219. Retrospective by roughly 30 years or more.
items.rights_basis: Same book and imprint as entry 598: Wingate, History of the Twenty-second Regiment of the National Guard of the State of New York, New York: E. W. Dayton, 1896; scan front matter 'COPYRIGHT, 1896 GENERAL GEORGE W. WINGATE'; IA metadata date 1896; Google Books 'E. W. Dayton, 1896', full view. Pre-1931, public domain.
items.evidence: Exact Google URL (pg=PA214) not fetched (robots.txt); bare page https://books.google.com/books?id=CJQQAAAAYAAJ was fetched by the probe (HTTP 200). Read the IA copy historyoftwenty00wing (item page HTTP 200; djvu.txt). The letter's text appears with running heads '216' and '219' (History of the Twenty-second Regiment); House Divided's transcription (hd.housedivided.dickinson.edu/node/40265) cites 'Wingate ... 1896, 214-219' and records 'Letter, C. Stuart Patterson to George W. Wingate, date unknown'. Claim 1, militiaman: Patterson was a sergeant commanding a gun of Landis' Philadelphia Battery with the Twenty-second New York and Gen. W. F. Smith's emergency force; the letter has them riding into the Carlisle market square at dusk to the cheers of the inhabitants and being served bread and coffee before the first shell. Claim 2, wounded: on p. 219 he says that just as he ordered the third shot, about ten or fifteen minutes into the action, he 'received the wound' that sent him to hospital and home two days later. The first three pages of the letter's start before 'about five miles from Carlisle' were not located separately (p. 214 start inferred from the House Divided citation). Leland's Memoirs (entry 602) names 'Stewart Patterson' in the same chapter and battery, which corroborates his presence.
items.extraction_notes: Adapter: archive-fulltext on historyoftwenty00wing (no page map; use running heads). The OCR garbles words ('Buttery', 'pcjppini;-'), so correct against the House Divided transcription as a cross-check only (it is a modern transcription). He wrote to Wingate who had already published an earlier description of the march (likely the 1864 pamphlet; this inference is not verified), so cross-read with Wingate's own text pp. 192-229 to avoid double counting. Tag as a humorous, anecdotal recollection by a gunner of the opening of the Union fire.
issues: Undated letter; composition date only bounded (after 1864, before 1896).
Anchor PA214 not fetchable on Google Books; supported via House Divided's citation and OCR running heads, not by seeing p. 214.
Humorous recollection; some details (distances, guns) unchecked against Smith's OR report.

summary: Batch 5 (the 12 queue entries whose "batch" field is 5: 649, 650, 652, 580, 581, 582, 583, 603, 607, 612, 615, 616) reviewed with real fetches. Every entry was identified as a real document and none is rejected. Verdicts: 8 APPROVE (649, 650, 652, 580, 583, 607, 612, 616; all tier A2 except 652 at A1), 3 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (581, 582, 603), 1 NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW (615, rights of a 1933 pamphlet). Descriptions were wrong or incomplete for 6 entries: 582 (the diary is not about Carlisle), 581, 607 (Stayman is not shown to be a professor), 612, 652 and, mildly, 649. All seven Dickinson links, plus the Hotchkiss and Sillers links, are dead or redirect to a generic page; for every one I fetched a Wayback or current-site replacement that matches. Perseus (entry 652) was not fetched; the same SHSP article was read in the Internet Archive scan. Reading note: the queue file's "batch" field is 1-based and I took the group with batch=5; the brief says "0-based", so if the other workers used array index 5 (batch=6: 620, 621, 624, 625, 636, 555, 556, 575, 584, 585, 610, 619) there is a gap at this batch and a duplicate at that one. Limits: Wayback copies of three Dickinson PDFs are cut at exactly 1 MiB, so parts of 581, 603 and 607 (letter 2) could not be read; handwriting was read only on a few pages; the Valley newspaper transcriptions were not compared with the scan PDFs; Perseus content and the Perseus-to-IA chapter mapping were not checked. Concurrent sibling agents may also have been hitting web.archive.org and archive.org; my own requests were at least 1.3 s apart per host.
systemic_findings: All seven Dickinson Archives links in this batch (580, 581, 582, 603, 607, 615, 616) are still 404 (http redirects to https, then 404); the new Dickinson site's navigation has no Civil War Resources section. Every one has a Wayback capture of the item page that matches the entry, and a Wayback capture of the item's PDF. The entries were copied from Cooper Wingert's House Divided guide Beyond Gettysburg (2018-06-11), whose own links point at the same dead URLs; the guide's descriptions were embellished in the list (for example a Dickinson professor for Stayman, which the guide does not say, and a Carlisle diary for Himes).

Wayback copies of three Dickinson PDFs (603, 581 and letter 2 of 607) are exactly 1,048,576 bytes, and the CDX record lengths of the captures are about 1.04 MB; the 603 file's own cross-reference pointer shows the original is larger than 1,063,206 bytes. So the Archive's captures of larger Dickinson PDFs are cut at 1 MiB, the full files are not recoverable from it, and any Dickinson PDF in other batches (620, 621, 624, 625) should be checked for a size of exactly 1,048,576 bytes before it is relied on. I rebuilt viewable files from the intact page images for 603 and 581; PyMuPDF alone would not open them.

The Valley of the Shadow moved: old valley.lib.virginia.edu/papers/{id} URLs redirect to the new site's home page (a generic redirect), but the same ids work at valley.newamericanhistory.org/letters/{id}, newspapers are at /newspapers/franklin-repository/YYYY/MM/DD, and the TEI and scan PDFs are at api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/... (newspapers/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.MM.DD.xml and newspapers_pdfs/... .pdf; HEAD returned 200 for the 15 and 29 July PDFs). The Valley's own copyright page restricts use to non-commercial purposes and the footer shows a CC BY-NC icon, and the TEI headers in the old edition claim copyright 2001 UVA, so Valley-hosted transcriptions cannot be A1; only the underlying 1863 text is public domain. Its newspaper pages give full text for only a few articles per issue; the rest are project-written summaries.

Notre Dame Rare Books: the old rarebooks.nd.edu/digital/civil_war/... paths redirect to the Rare Books home page, and the same path on rarebooks.library.nd.edu returns 403 Access Denied; Wayback holds the item pages and collection indexes. Transcriptions carry a Notre Dame copyright footer.

Perseus replacement method for the SHSP entries: Internet Archive scans follow the pattern southernhistoric{vol}{yy}sout (vol. 28 is southernhistoric2819sout), each with an _djvu.txt OCR file and a _page_numbers.json that maps leaves to printed pages (printed pp. 148-155 are leaves 162-169). The plan's SRC-08 lists other volumes of the same family but not vol. 28; metadata says reviewed by UF staff and out of copyright.

Descriptions in this list are unreliable on place and date even when the document is real: 582 (Himes diary) is about New Oxford, Hanover and the Gettysburg approaches, not Carlisle; 581 (Himes letter) was written from New Oxford and its readable pages do not cover the shelling; 612 is a post-campaign letter; 652 spans March to June, not June only. The verifier brief's rule to read two concrete claims per entry caught these.

Rights: none of the entries in this batch from Dickinson, the Valley or Notre Dame is A1. The underlying 1863 documents are public domain, but each host reserves rights over its scans or transcriptions, so A2 holds, and where the only retrievable text is a modern typed transcription (582, 603) I limited use to link-out and facts. The only A1 is the 1900 SHSP volume (652). A 1933 pamphlet (615) is neither A1 nor safely public domain without a notice and renewal check.

Operational: the shared scratchpad is used by several agents; another agent overwrote a helper file I had written there, so I worked in my own subdirectory (scratchpad/sv2b5) and used the repo's PoliteClient (honest user agent, robots.txt obeyed) with at least 1.3 s between requests per host; sibling agents may have been using web.archive.org and archive.org at the same time. Nothing under legacy/ or the other workflow's paths was touched, no browser was launched, and I wrote no files in the repo.

items.written: 1863-07-15 (weekly issue; contents dated June 21 to July 14, 1863)
items.rights_basis: The text is a Chambersburg weekly published 15 July 1863 (date in the page and in the TEI file), so public domain by date. The host layer is not free of conditions: the Valley of the Shadow Copyright and Fair Use Statement says the site is free for non-commercial research, teaching and private study, that some material may still be under copyright, and asks for citation; every page footer carries an icon linking to the CC BY-NC 4.0 deed (icon only, no page-level licence text found). The project-written Summary, Excerpt and Names fields are its own work. The newspaper TEI header has no rights statement. The non-commercial limit needs a human decision before verbatim reuse.
items.evidence: GET of https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/newspapers/franklin-repository/1863/07/15 returned HTTP 200, 384,777 bytes, title Franklin Repository: July 15, 1863 (Newspapers, The Valley of the Shadow); host robots.txt is 404 (no rules) and the api host robots.txt has an empty Disallow. Page 1 (THE INVASION!) reprints Lee's General Orders No. 72 (21 June), Ewell's General Orders No. 49 (22 June) and Ewell's Chambersburg orders of 24 June, then reports the burning of Thaddeus Stevens's Iron Works, the killing of a farmer named Strite near Chambersburg and the bombardment of Carlisle, so both concrete claims in the description check out. Pages 2 and 4 also carry long Gettysburg battle reprints (a Philadelphia Inquirer account of 1 July, Richmond papers, a piece on the Pennsylvania Reserves) that the description omits. Cross-check: the historian's OR index holds General Orders No. 72 signed by R. H. Chilton, 21 June, at OR 27/3 p. 912 (or27-3:p0912.3), so the Repository reprint is a second witness of an order we already have. The TEI file api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/.../fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.15.xml (141,258 bytes) fetched; a PDF of the scanned issue answers a HEAD request (200 application/pdf) but was not downloaded or compared with the transcription.
items.extraction_notes: Use the TEI transcript elements (one per article) or the page's Full Text of Article blocks, never the project-written Summary, Excerpt or Names in Announcement fields. Only 7 articles in this issue have full text; the rest have summaries only. Keep [illegible] and [sic] markers; the page records tape-obscured text. Attribute reprints to the paper they came from (Inquirer, Herald, Richmond Enquirer and Whig, Savannah Republican). Prefer the OR for the Lee and Ewell orders. Spot-check quotes against the issue PDF.
issues: Description covers only page 1; the issue also holds a long Gettysburg battle section reprinted from other papers, so relevance is campaign and battle.
Most items in the issue have project summaries but no transcription.
Battle accounts are second-hand reprints from other papers, not the Repository's own reporting.
Lee's and Ewell's orders duplicate the Official Records and add no new text.
Non-commercial and attribution terms on the host's transcription.

items.written: 1863-07-29 (weekly issue; includes a correspondent's sketch dated Gettysburg, 15 July 1863)
items.rights_basis: A Chambersburg weekly published 29 July 1863 (date on the page), so public domain by date. Same host terms as entry 649: the Valley of the Shadow Copyright and Fair Use Statement (free for non-commercial use, some material may still be under copyright, cite the source), a CC BY-NC 4.0 icon in the footer, and project-written summaries that are not public domain. The newspaper TEI header carries no rights statement.
items.evidence: GET of https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/newspapers/franklin-repository/1863/07/29 returned HTTP 200, 340,929 bytes, title Franklin Repository: July 29, 1863. Both parts of the description were read and confirmed. Page 2 has a full-text article on visiting the Gettysburg battlefield and its hospitals on the Tuesday after the fight and a correspondent's sketch (dateline Gettysburg, 15 July 1863) of Gen. S. W. Crawford and the Pennsylvania Reserves with the 5th Corps on 2 and 3 July. Page 8 reports the death of Col. Benjamin F. Carter, 4th Texas, from Gettysburg wounds at the Academy hospital in Chambersburg and lists the town's hospitals, one of them a school house for wounded Confederates. Page 1 reprints Confederate newspaper comment on the retreat. The page links a TEI file and a scan PDF (api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.29.xml and the matching newspapers_pdfs/...pdf); I fetched the 15 July TEI only and did not download or compare either scan.
items.extraction_notes: Same method as entry 649: TEI transcript elements or Full Text blocks per article, excluding the project's Summary and Excerpt fields. 6 articles carry full text; most others are summaries only. Tape-obscured text on page 1 appears as [illegible]. The Pennsylvania Reserves and Gettysburg battlefield pieces are the battle-relevant items. The hospital items are Chambersburg aftermath.
issues: The issue is battle aftermath and campaign context rather than fighting; only the Reserves sketch narrates 2 and 3 July.
Full text exists for only a few articles.
The Reserves account is a second-hand witness sketch passed on by a correspondent.
Non-commercial and attribution terms on the host's transcription.

items.written: 1900 (SHSP vol. 28, printed pp. 148-155; abstracts of correspondence dated March to 30 June 1863)
items.rights_basis: Imprint year read from the title page of the Internet Archive scan: Richmond, Va., published by the Society, 1900, printed by Wm. Ellis Jones. Archive metadata for item southernhistoric2819sout (University of Florida Smathers Libraries scan, 2015) marks the copyright status as reviewed by UF staff and out of copyright. It is an original imprint, not a reprint. The abstracts quote U.S. Government records.
items.evidence: The Perseus link was not fetched because www.perseus.tufts.edu/robots.txt disallows all paths (earlier probe). I reviewed the Internet Archive scan instead. archive.org/metadata/southernhistoric2819sout returned HTTP 200: volume 28 (1900), 408 images, scanned 2015-04-24. The OCR text (southernhistoric2819sout_djvu.txt, 1,077,008 bytes) has the table of contents entry XVII, The Correspondence of General R. E. Lee, Chancellorsville to Gettysburg, March to August 1863, by Colonel Wm. H. Palmer, p. 148, and the article itself, whose editor's preface is by R. A. Brock. The page-number map puts printed pp. 148-155 on IA leaves 162-169. The article is a calendar of abstracts citing OR vol. 25 pt. 2 and vol. 27 pt. 3 pages, with entries to and from Davis, Seddon, Cooper, Stuart, A. P. Hill, D. H. Hill, Jenkins and Pickett, and a closing note on p. 155 saying Davis's letter of 28 June was carried by a courier captured by a member of Meade's staff. Cross-check against the historian's OR 27/3 index: Lee to Davis, 9 June, p. 874; Lee to Stuart, 22 June, p. 913; Lee to Davis, 23 June, p. 924; Lee to Davis, Williamsport, 25 June, pp. 930-931; Jenkins to D. H. Hill, 20 June, p. 908, all exist as cited. The description is partly wrong: the calendar starts in March and runs to 30 June, covers more than the Davis letters, and has nothing from July or August despite its title.
items.extraction_notes: Use the IA archive-fulltext adapter on leaves 162-169 (printed pp. 148-155). The OCR is noisy in the italic date and page-cite column (for example i86j for 1863), so every quoted date and OR page cite must be checked against the page image. The words are mostly one-line abstracts of OR documents, so the text adds little that the OR does not already hold. The editor's preface and Palmer's framing are Lost Cause argument and are better used for perspective than as evidence.
issues: The listed Perseus URL was not checked; the mapping of its chapter 1.16 to this article is unverified.
Title of the article is longer than the entry and spans March to August 1863, not just June.
Not only dispatches to Davis; many addressees.
The Davis letter of 28 June appears only as a short note on the last page.
Almost all of the content duplicates OR vol. 25 pt. 2 and vol. 27 pt. 3, which we already ingest.
The compiler (Palmer, A. P. Hill's former chief of staff) wrote it in 1900 to support the supply and cavalry shortage argument, so it is retrospective advocacy.

items.written: Published 1863-07-18 in The Methodist (date from Dickinson's cover sheet and item page); describes 27 June to 1 July 1863
items.rights_basis: An 1863 newspaper article, public domain by date. The only copy found is the host's PDF of column images, and Dickinson's pages carry a copyright notice reserving all rights, with no licence statement for its scans. A faithful scan of a public domain item adds little, but the host's terms need a human check.
items.evidence: The listed URL still returns HTTP 404 (archives.dickinson.edu, after an http to https redirect); the Civil War Resources section is gone from the host's navigation. The Wayback capture 20231207203932 of the item page fetched (HTTP 200, 21,712 bytes): item The Methodist, A Few Days Under Rebel Rule, July 18, 1863, 11 pages, people tags Hillman, Fitzhugh Lee, Jenkins and others. The Wayback copy of its PDF (capture 20240620182759, 3,555,300 bytes, 11 pages) is a cover sheet plus 10 pages of newspaper column images with no text layer. I read the columns: the byline is Prof. S. D. Hillman, Carlisle; sections cover the rebel entrance into Carlisle, a Discussion with Rebel Officers (Maj. Pendleton of Ewell's staff and a topographical officer, on providence, the aims of the South, all the slave states, and the freeing of slaves), the appearance of Jenkins's cavalry and an infantry brigade in the college grounds, a rebel chaplain's talk, and requisitions on the stores. This confirms the description, though slavery is one thread in a broader argument about the war.
items.extraction_notes: Image-only, so manual transcription from the 10 column images, then a second-person check. Use the Wayback PDF capture (https://web.archive.org/web/20240620182759/https://archives.dickinson.edu/sites/all/files/files_war/1863-07-18_rebel_rule.pdf). Ingest state would be blocked:manual-transcription. The columns carry no masthead, so confirm the periodical and date against The Methodist itself if the date matters.
issues: Listed host link is dead (404); use the Wayback capture of the item page.
PDF is images only; the periodical name and date rest on Dickinson's own cover sheet and item page.
Host's all-rights-reserved footer.
The Methodist was a New York paper; the article was written by a Carlisle civilian about 2 to 3 weeks after the events.

items.rights_basis: A private letter of 1863; the writer was an adult then, so any copyright term has long expired (his death year not checked). The only retrievable form is a partial image copy hosted by Dickinson under an all-rights-reserved notice, and the typed transcript the item page mentions is not in the part of the file that could be recovered.
items.evidence: Listed URL still 404. Wayback capture 20150919055535 of the item page fetched (21,452 bytes): Letter from Charles F. Himes to Ogden N. Rood, October 2, 1863, 13 pages, events tagged Battle of Gettysburg, Invasion of Carlisle and Invasion of Pennsylvania (no Shelling of Carlisle tag), Himes a Dickinson figure. Its PDF exists only as one Wayback capture (20240225221947, files_war/mc2000-01_b10_f10.pdf) and my copy is exactly 1,048,576 bytes, cut off; 2 of its 3 recoverable JPEG pages decode and the third is cut. I read both handwritten pages: the letter is headed New Oxford, Adams Co., Pa., Oct 2nd 1863, Dear Rood; Himes says he was at Carlisle for Commencement about 25 June, helped inspect the militia defences, left for home that evening and reached it about 11 p.m., then describes the Confederates entering Gettysburg on Friday 26 June. So the legible part does not describe the occupation or shelling of Carlisle as seen by him, which contradicts the description. Pages 3 to 13 could not be read.
items.extraction_notes: No verbatim use: the full document is not retrievable (Wayback copy cut at 1 MiB, host gone) and it is handwriting. Link-out to the Wayback item page; use facts and dates only after a human reads the complete letter, or ask Dickinson Archives for the PDF.
issues: Description says the letter describes the occupation and shelling of Carlisle; the readable pages cover pre-occupation Carlisle, the trip home and the Confederate arrival at Gettysburg.
Writer is described as a Carlisle civilian but wrote from New Oxford, Adams County.
Written 3 months after the events.
Wayback PDF truncated at 1 MiB (3 of 13 pages' images recoverable).
Dead listed link.

items.written: 1863-06-23 to 1863-07-03 (the part retrievable; partial typed transcript of an 1863 pocket diary)
items.rights_basis: The 1863 diary is old enough to be public domain (writer's death year not checked), but the only text retrievable is Dickinson's typed partial transcript with gaps and hand corrections, on a site that reserves all rights. No images of the manuscript are in the PDF, so the transcription cannot be checked against the original.
items.evidence: Listed URL still 404. Wayback capture 20240302072813 of the item page fetched (22,446 bytes): Pocket Diary of Charles F. Himes, 1863, 3 pages, partial transcript, Dickinson says a complete transcript is not yet available. Its PDF (capture 20240620182659, 968,550 bytes, intact) is a cover sheet and two typed transcript pages (text layer plus scan), which I read. Entries: 23 to 25 June in Carlisle for the alumni meeting and Commencement, leaving on the 25th as the rebels approached; 27 June at New Oxford where about 3,000 infantry of Gordon's brigade, Early's division, passed through; 30 June cannonading toward Hanover and a stay there; 1 July walking toward Gettysburg, picketed by Confederates, seeing their ambulances carry off the dead and wounded; 3 July heavy firing and leaving for fear of a flank movement. The transcript stops on 3 July. So the description (a day-by-day diary of the Confederate presence in Carlisle) is wrong for the text that exists: the Confederates it records are at New Oxford, near Hanover and near Gettysburg.
items.extraction_notes: Treat as an Adams County civilian view of 27 June to 3 July, not as a Carlisle source. The typed text has blanks, strike-throughs and hand corrections, so no quote without a second reader; the day order in the 26 and 27 June entries should be checked against the manuscript, since the destruction of the railroad bridge and warehouse is more often dated to 26 June at Gettysburg. Full diary not available; ask Dickinson Archives.
issues: Description names the wrong place (Carlisle); the readable entries are New Oxford, Hanover and the Gettysburg approaches.
Dickinson's own tags also say Shelling of Carlisle, which the transcript does not support.
Partial transcript only (3 July at the end); the item page says a complete one does not exist.
Typed text is modern work with gaps; no manuscript images to verify against.
Dead listed link.

items.rights_basis: A letter written in 1863 (public domain by date; the author's death year was not checked here). The electronic edition's TEI header states Copyright 2001 by the Rector and Visitors of the University of Virginia and that the text is used with permission from the Library of Congress; the new site's footer links a CC BY-NC 4.0 deed. The transcription's terms and the scope of the Library of Congress permission need a human check.
items.evidence: The listed URL http://valley.lib.virginia.edu/papers/A4042 now redirects to the Valley of the Shadow home page (HTTP 200, 178,202 bytes), a generic page. The same document is live at https://valley.newamericanhistory.org/letters/A4042 (HTTP 200, 166,712 bytes): Augusta County: Jedediah Hotchkiss to Sara A. Hotchkiss, June 28, 1863. The letter is headed Hd. Qrs. 2nd Corps A.N.V., Carlisle, Pa., and tells of the quiet occupation of Carlisle on 27 June, troops in the U.S. Barracks and the Dickinson College yard, a requisition on the town for medicines and supplies, a Sunday sermon by Mr. Lacy and the temper of the townspeople, which matches the summary. The TEI file (api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/papers/A4042.xml) names the Library of Congress Hotchkiss Collection, Reel 4, as the source copy and shows no page images. Hotchkiss as Second Corps map-maker rests on the House Divided guide (Wingert, 2018), which I fetched, plus the letterhead.
items.extraction_notes: Use the TEI or the page's Original tab, not the Modern Spelling tab or the summary and keyword fields. The page text shows both versions, so deduplicate. No scan on this site: a verbatim check needs the Library of Congress manuscript reel. Short document (about 4 manuscript pages).
issues: Old UVA URL now lands on a generic page; use the new letters URL.
Page shows the text twice (original spelling and modern spelling).
No page images on the host, so the transcription cannot be checked there.
Edition copyright and Library of Congress permission note.

items.written: 1863-06-12 to 1863-07-15 read (item page says to 18 July); a modern typed transcription of the diary
items.rights_basis: The diary is an 1863 manuscript (author's death year not checked), but the only copy retrievable is a modern typed transcription with editor's notes and an appendix reference, held by a host that reserves all rights; who made it and under what terms is unknown. That transcription is probably a copyright claim of its own.
items.evidence: Listed URL still 404. Wayback capture 20231210113055 of the item page fetched (22,113 bytes): Isaac Harris Diary, U.S. Sanitary Commission, June 12 to July 18, 1863, 16 pages, a transcript of part of the diary (gift of Caroline Harris Baldwin); Dickinson says a complete copy is at the Army Heritage and Education Center. Its PDF capture (20220518060218) is exactly 1,048,576 bytes: the file's own cross-reference pointer shows the original is larger than 1,063,206 bytes, and the CDX lengths of both captures (about 1.04 MB) match, so Wayback holds only a cut copy. It has no text layer (bilevel images). I rebuilt the 15 intact page images into a readable PDF and read printed pp. 5, 13 to 18. The entry for Wednesday 1 July (printed p. 13) puts the writer in Carlisle during the Confederate shelling and says he took quarters under the lee of the jail wall with Smith and Gowan, which confirms the listed claim; the entries for 5 to 7 July (printed p. 15) have him walking into Carlisle in rain to the hospital in Dickinson College and arranging stores for it. The last page (printed p. 19) decodes blank and the appendix is missing.
items.extraction_notes: Image-only, with the full file not retrievable; at most a link-out plus facts and dates until a human obtains the complete transcript from Dickinson or the Army Heritage and Education Center and settles the rights. The diary uses period racial language that needs careful handling.
issues: Wayback copy cut at exactly 1 MiB; printed p. 19 and the appendix are missing.
Text is a modern transcription with an editor's notes, not the manuscript.
Host's all-rights-reserved notice.
Description says the writer worked with the wounded; what the legible pages show is hospital supply work.
Dead listed link.

items.rights_basis: Two private letters of 1863 (writer an adult then; any copyright term long expired, death year not checked). The copies are held and scanned by Dickinson, whose pages reserve all rights; the typed transcript beside the first letter is the host's work.
items.evidence: The listed URL (a people page for Stayman) still returns 404. Wayback capture 20231130070857 of it (19,658 bytes) lists two letters from John Keagy Stayman to Edgar E. Hastings. Captures of the two item pages fetched: 20240731222132 (July 1863, 6 pages) and 20240719132709 (13 Aug 1863, 5 pages). The PDF of letter 1 (capture 20240630002255, 3,108,759 bytes, intact) holds a cover sheet, 4 pages of handwriting images and a typed transcript page; I read the transcript and the first handwritten page. It is headed Baltimore, July 1863: Stayman says he made a quick visit to Carlisle to see the damage done by the rebel occupation and shelling, stopped at a Philadelphia hospital with brothers in the medical service where Gettysburg wounded had arrived, describes the college hospital as temporary, the barracks as a heap of ruins and the coming draft, and congratulates Hastings on a Latin prize. The PDF of letter 2 (capture 20240624092903) is cut at exactly 1,048,576 bytes and does not open. Nothing fetched calls Stayman a professor, and the Latin prize, vacation and Fall Session wording read like a student's or former student's; the House Divided guide calls him a civilian.
items.extraction_notes: Take letter 1 from the 4 handwriting images, with the typed transcript as a cross-check (my check of the transcript against the image covered the opening lines only and was inconclusive on one date). Letter 2 is only partly retrievable; a human should obtain a full copy. Both letters are second-hand about the occupation and shelling: the writer was in Baltimore and visited Carlisle afterwards.
issues: Description says a Dickinson professor; nothing supports that and the content suggests a student or former student.
The listed link is a people index page covering two letters, not one document.
Letter 2's Wayback PDF is cut at 1 MiB.
Content is post-occupation and second-hand, so aftermath rather than campaign.
Dead listed link.

items.rights_basis: An 1863 letter by an author who died in 1863 per the collection introduction (1838 to 1863), so public domain by date. The transcription is credited to two University of Notre Dame staff (2004 to 2006) and the page footer reads Copyright 2006, 2009, 2011, Department of Special Collections, University of Notre Dame; no licence is stated for the transcription or the scans.
items.evidence: The listed URL (rarebooks.nd.edu/.../sillers-holmes/5025-12.shtml) returns 200 only after a redirect to the Rare Books home page (a generic landing page), and the same path on the new host rarebooks.library.nd.edu returns 403 Access Denied. Wayback capture 20231211132213 fetched (34,933 bytes): Sillers-Holmes Family Correspondence, August 7, 1863, MSN/CW 5025-12, autograph letter, William W. Sillers to his sister Frances Sillers Holmes, near Orange Court House, 4 pages with page images at 3 resolutions. In it he mentions a servant who joined plunderers at Gettysburg, a mess chest lost at Waterloo Gap, three days at the Carlisle Barracks, and Fitzhugh Lee burning those buildings. The Wayback capture of the collection index (20241013135840, 60,121 bytes) says Sillers (1838 to 1863) was a Confederate officer of the 30th North Carolina and lists 14 of his letters, including 10 July and 31 July 1863 ones nearer the campaign. The listed letter is therefore a post-campaign letter, not one written during the campaign.
items.extraction_notes: Short HTML transcription (about 5.7 KB of text) with page images; use the transcription block per page and check against the images. Spelling and punctuation follow the original. Letters 5025-10 (16 July) and 5025-11 (31 July) are closer in time to the campaign and may be worth adding as separate entries.
issues: Described as from the campaign but it is dated 7 August 1863, five weeks after the retreat.
Old host path redirects to a generic page; the new host does not serve it.
Transcription copyright notice.
A letter that mentions a servant and enslaved people: needs careful framing.

items.written: Letter written July 1932 (Hereford, England), read 24 February 1933, printed as a 1933 pamphlet
items.rights_basis: Imprint year 1933, so the pre-1931 rule for A1 does not apply. The OCR text of the pamphlet contains no copyright notice, which would put a 1933 US publication in the public domain, but I did not confirm that on the page images, did not check renewal records and have no archive metadata saying so; Dickinson reserves all rights on its copy. A human or counsel needs to settle this.
items.evidence: Listed URL still 404. Wayback capture 20231002015237 of the item page fetched (20,592 bytes): Boyhood Memories of the Civil War 1861-65, Invasion of Carlisle, James W. Sullivan, 46 pages, publisher Hamilton Library Association, Carlisle. The PDF capture (20240622030747, 14,654,048 bytes, 46 pages, OCR text layer of 106,434 characters) has a title page: a letter written by James W. Sullivan in July 1932 at Hereford, England, to Jane Van Ness Smead of Carlisle, read before the Hamilton Library Association on 24 February 1933 by John M. Rhey, 1933. The text is a recollection by a boy of 13 to 17 and recounts the occupation and the night shelling, and says he heard his first shell while he was at a patriotic task; Ewell's corps is mentioned on page 41. The word copyright appears 0 times in the OCR text. The description is accurate; the Dickinson date field (July 1932) is the letter date, not the imprint year.
items.extraction_notes: The Wayback PDF is complete and has an OCR text layer, but the OCR is noisy (garbled characters and broken words), so quotes would need checking against the page images. The text is long (46 pages) and mostly general recollection; the shelling passages are around PDF pages 22 to 38. The writer uses a racial slur in an anecdote about a childhood playmate; handle with care.
issues: Rights tier unresolved (1933 imprint, no notice seen in the OCR, not checked on images or renewal records).
Written about 69 years after the events: memory and hindsight, not contemporaneous.
Dead listed link; PDF only on Wayback.
Host's all-rights-reserved footer.

items.rights_basis: An anonymous printed broadside of 1863 (dateline Carlisle, July 3, 1863 on the sheet), public domain by date. The only copy is Dickinson's scan, hosted under an all-rights-reserved notice with no licence statement; a scan of a public domain print adds little, but the host's terms need a human check.
items.evidence: Listed URL still 404. Wayback capture 20240223194400 of the item page fetched (20,707 bytes): Broadside of Citizens of Cumberland Valley, Call to Arms, July 3, 1863, 2 pages, event tags Battle of Gettysburg and Shelling of Carlisle. Its PDF (capture 20240329143726, 369,941 bytes, intact) is a cover sheet and one scanned page (1011 by 1376 pixels) with a poor OCR text layer. I viewed the bottom of the scan: it ends with a paragraph saying printing was interrupted on Wednesday evening by the invaders' cannon before Carlisle, shells coming through the tree-tops and into houses, an appeal to report to Harrisburg and enlist for the war, and the dateline Carlisle, July 3, 1863, Circulate through the county. This confirms a recruitment appeal issued during the battle, with a short eyewitness note on the shelling of 1 July.
items.extraction_notes: Transcribe from the image (the OCR layer is too poor to use), then have a second person check. Short text, about 3,500 characters. Anonymous, so attribute to the sheet, not a person. Ingest state would be blocked:manual-transcription.
issues: OCR text layer unusable; the one digit of the date is partly damaged on the scan but agrees with Dickinson's metadata.
Anonymous partisan appeal, not a neutral report.
Host's all-rights-reserved notice.
Dead listed link.

summary: Batch index 4 (0-based) of data-src/sources-v2/qc/review-queue-next.json is the object labelled "batch": 5 (ranks 49-60; entries 649, 650, 652, 580, 581, 582, 583, 603, 607, 612, 615, 616), which matches review_priority.batch=5 on entry 649 in registry.json. The file's own labels are 1-based, so "batch number 4" read literally would be ranks 37-48 (628..648); I followed the explicit "0-based". Results: 12 items, 7 APPROVE (all rights tier A2 except 652 at A1; every A2 needs a human rights decision before any quote), 5 APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (607, 612, 615 at the end; 580 and 616 are APPROVE with manual transcription). Wait, recount: APPROVE = 649, 650, 652, 580, 581, 582, 583, 603, 616 (9); APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY = 607, 612, 615 (3); NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW = 0; REJECT = 0. Descriptions: accurate 8 (649, 650, 580, 583, 603, 607, 615, 616), partly inaccurate 3 (652, 582, 612), inaccurate 1 (581). Where the listed link was dead or generic I found a fetched replacement for every item. Method: read robots.txt, one request per second per host, honest Gettysburg-sources-QC user agent through tools/sources-qc/lib/http.mjs (cached under tmp/sources-v2/cache); no browser; Perseus was not fetched; ehistory and HathiTrust were not touched. Scratch files stayed in the session scratchpad. Not verified: Dickinson's rights terms beyond the footer notice (I found no reuse or licence page); the page-level text of the Stayman July 1863 letter (Wayback PDF truncated); Himes's and Harris's death dates; the second Internet Archive scan of SHSP vol. 28 (southernhistoric0028sout) was only checked at the metadata level.
systemic_findings: Part IX of the list appears to be built from one Dickinson House Divided blog post, 'Beyond Gettysburg: Primary Sources for the Gettysburg Campaign' (housedivided.dickinson.edu, WordPress post 4972, published 2018-06-11, modified 2018-09-14, fetched via its wp-json endpoint). Every Dickinson, Valley, Notre Dame and Hotchkiss URL in this batch matches a link in that post, and some list descriptions repeat the post's blurbs (Hillman 'debated Confederate officers about slavery'; Harris 'under the lee of the jail wall'). The post's own captions were therefore treated as descriptions. Reading the documents contradicted the list in 3 of 12 entries (581 and 582 Himes: not about the occupation of Carlisle, and written/kept mostly outside Carlisle; 612 Sillers: written 7 Aug, not 'from the campaign'). Unreviewed Part IX descriptions that came from the same post are suspect for the same reason.

The Dickinson Archives site was rebuilt (Drupal 10). All seven legacy paths in this batch (/civil-war-resources/..., /civil-war/..., /civil-war-people/...) return 404, and guessed new-style paths (/document-descriptions/<same slug>) also 404. The new pattern is /document-descriptions/<slug> and /archives-people/<slug> with PDFs under /sites/default/files/files_document/. Of my seven Dickinson items only the Stayman 13 Aug 1863 letter has a live page on the new site (found through https://archives.dickinson.edu/archives-people/stayman-john-keagy). The rest exist only as Wayback captures (item pages 2015-2024, PDFs 2022-2024). The owner may want to email archives@dickinson.edu for current locations and permission terms; I sent nothing.

Wayback PDF captures can be truncated. Two PDFs in this batch (Isaac Harris diary I-BaldwinC-1998-1.pdf, capture 20220518060218; Stayman July letter I-MachemerA-1975-1.pdf, capture 20230924161936) stop at exactly 1,048,576 bytes with no trailer: MuPDF opens them with 0 pages. I recovered the Harris text layer by inflating the page content streams (all 15 transcript pages), but the last page image and the later pages of the Stayman July letter are not captured. The registry's candidate-replacement check compared item-page titles only, never the PDFs; a capture of an item page is not proof that its PDF is there (for entry 581 the 2015 capture's PDF is not archived at all; a 2024 capture of a differently named PDF path is).

Registry candidate-title checks can mislabel good replacements. Entry 583's Wayback capture was flagged 'title unclear (overlap 0.00)' but is the right letter: the Valley title is 'Augusta County: Jedediah Hotchkiss to Sara A. Hotchkiss, June 28, 1863'. Title overlap should not be the gate.

Valley of the Shadow moved: old valley.lib.virginia.edu/papers/<ID> now redirects to the new site's home page (a dead link in disguise), but valley.newamericanhistory.org/papers/<ID> redirects to /letters/<ID> and works (verified for A4042). Newspaper issues have a clean structured source at api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers/fr1863/<file>.xml (api host robots.txt allows all). The Valley site says it is free for non-commercial research, teaching, scholarship and private study, warns that some materials may still be under copyright, and its footer links an icon to CC BY-NC 4.0; the Hotchkiss TEI header says copyright 2001 Rector and Visitors of the University of Virginia and 'used with permission from Library of Congress'. Treat every Valley item as tier A2 with a non-commercial condition, not A1.

Notre Dame: every legacy rarebooks.nd.edu/digital/civil_war/... URL answers 301 to the Rare Books home page (HTTP 200, no letter). The collection now lives on marble.nd.edu (Sillers-Holmes: https://marble.nd.edu/item/MSNCW5025_EAD), as images plus metadata; the item pages I read show no transcription text, and the JSON-LD names RARE as copyright holder. The only transcription I could read is the old page in the Wayback Machine.

Perseus is disallowed by robots.txt, so entry 652 was verified on the Internet Archive scan southernhistoric2819sout (University of Florida scan, 1900 imprint, archive metadata 'Out of copyright'). The Archive also holds southernhistoric0028rabr, a 1991 Broadfoot reprint of vol. 28, which must stay off any allow-list; and southernhistoric0028sout, a second scan I did not read.

Search-engine snippets (WebSearch) were used only to discover URLs; every claim in the items rests on a page, PDF or file I fetched. One snippet claimed the Hillman article first ran in the Hollidaysburg Register; I could not confirm it and did not use it.

items.rights_basis: The newspaper is an 1863 US imprint (public domain), but the text is the Valley of the Shadow transcription. valley.newamericanhistory.org/about/copyright (fetched) says the site is free for non-commercial research, teaching, scholarship and private study, that some materials may still be under copyright, and that users answer for their own uses; the page footer carries an icon linking to creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/ with no visible text; the issue XML header has no availability statement. A non-commercial condition means a human must decide before any quote is shipped. The project's summaries, keywords and names fields are its own text and are not usable.
items.evidence: Fetched the listed URL (200; body read; response cached from the 2026-09-30 probe). Page 1 column 1 is a long article headed The Invasion that reprints Lee's General Orders No. 72 (21 June), Ewell's General Orders No. 49 (22 June) and Ewell's Chambersburg orders of 24 June, then local abuses (Strite murder, Stevens' Works) and a Bombardment of Carlisle item, so the list's description is accurate. Page 2 also carries 'The Battle of Gettysburg', reprinted from the Philadelphia Inquirer of 7 July and Richmond papers, which the list does not mention. Fetched the structured source behind the page, api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.15.xml (200, 141,258 bytes, sha256 71fcadc2f7a9af7d15992c2bb08b247a97d77500445556fee5dd620577c84f4c): 8 pages, 33 article divisions, 17 [illegible] markers, tagger 'Sally Henninger, 1st pass' only. The cached probe's page title is 'Franklin Repository: July 15, 1863' and the XML id is fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.15.
items.extraction_notes: Use the XML (page, column, head, excerpt, transcript per article) rather than the Nuxt HTML, which embeds the text as escaped JSON. Segment by article division; skip the project's Summary, Names in Announcement and Excerpt fields. Expect [illegible] gaps and a first-pass-only transcription (no second pass recorded). The pasted General Orders No. 72 duplicates OR vol. 27 pt. 3 p. 912, already ingested: cross-check rather than double count. The page 2 battle articles are second-hand reprints; tag them as such. Segment boundaries inside page 1 column 1 (one long editorial compilation) need care.
issues: List description covers only the page 1 compilation; the issue also prints second-hand battle reports on page 2.
Transcription is first pass only with 17 illegible gaps.
Valley rights position (non-commercial use; CC BY-NC icon) conflicts with any commercial reuse: hold for rights review.
Scope: newspaper compilation weeks after the events; not contemporaneous in the same-day sense.

items.rights_basis: Same as 649: an 1863 US newspaper (public domain) presented through the Valley of the Shadow transcription, whose copyright statement allows non-commercial use only, warns some materials may still be under copyright, and whose footer icon links to CC BY-NC 4.0. Human rights decision needed before quoting.
items.evidence: Fetched the listed URL (200, cached probe, body read) and the XML at api.valley.newamericanhistory.org/storage/data/newspapers/fr1863/pa.fr.fr.1863.07.29.xml (200, 110,276 bytes, sha256 dea3d35a7da6faace329dff98c07c80204e61c0104e8db0ca43dd66cc7f0cdd3; 8 pages, 51 article divisions, 16 [illegible] markers, taggers 'Sally Henninger, 1st pass; Susanna Michele Lee, 2nd pass'). Claim 1, Pennsylvania Reserves: page 2 column 2 carries a correspondence dated Gettysburg, 15 July 1863, relaying a witness's sketch of Crawford's division: it reached the field about 11 a.m. on 2 July, lay in reserve with the Fifth Corps, went in late that afternoon, and on the 3rd advanced from the hill (146th New York named). Claim 2, hospitals: page 8 has local items on Col. Benjamin F. Carter, 4th Texas, dying at the Academy hospital in Chambersburg, and a list of three hospitals (Academy, Town Hall, School House for Confederate wounded) per the project's summaries (I did not read the full text of those short items). Also on page 2 column 1: a writer's visit to the Gettysburg battlefield on the Tuesday evening after the fight, with hospital scenes; page 1 prints Richmond and Charleston papers' comments, including on Lee's retreat.
items.extraction_notes: Same XML path as 649. The Reserves piece and the battlefield-visit piece are the high-value segments for the battle; keep them separate from the page 8 local-news items. Mark the Reserves account as a relayed, unnamed witness, written about 12 days later. Skip project summaries and name lists. Valley's summary garbles the general's name (reads Wylie for S. Wylie Crawford): do not copy summaries.
issues: The 'sketch of the Pennsylvania Reserves' is a relayed anonymous witness account dated 15 July, not a signed eyewitness report.
Hospital material is short local news on page 8, not a main article.
Valley summary misnames the general (metadata error).
Rights: non-commercial condition, hold for review.

items.written: 1900 (SHSP vol. 28, pp. 148-155); compiled from OR Ser. I vol. 25 pt. 2 and vol. 27 pt. 3 (letters March-June 1863)
items.rights_basis: US imprint before 1931: the Internet Archive scan southernhistoric2819sout (University of Florida Smathers Libraries, scanned 2015-04-24, 408 images) opens with a title page reading Southern Historical Society Papers, Volume XXVIII, ed. R. A. Brock, Richmond, published by the Society, 1900; archive.org/metadata says possible-copyright-status 'Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright'. The 1991 Broadfoot reprint (southernhistoric0028rabr) is not the same edition and is not covered.
items.evidence: The Perseus link was not fetched (robots.txt Disallow: / per the registry probe). I read the same article in the Internet Archive scan: downloaded southernhistoric2819sout_djvu.txt (1,077,008 bytes, sha256 8467b13f01c1608d4fc32b044963722889ee5636fba7655097402b18fc80ebef) and the page_numbers.json folio map. The table of contents lists XVII 'The Correspondence of General R. E. Lee. Chancellorsville to Gettysburg, March to August, 1863', by Col. Wm. H. Palmer, p. 148; the article runs pp. 148-155 (leaves 162-169, 1-based) and is a table of abstracts of Lee, Davis, Seddon, Cooper, Jenkins and Pickett correspondence with OR page references, framed by an editor's note and a closing note about Davis's 28 June letter to Lee, said to have been carried by a courier captured by Capt. Dahlgren, and a line that Lee resigned in August. Cross-check: I compared the OR references in Palmer's table with the historian's OR vol. 27 pt. 3 dispatch index (historian-src/corpus/or27/dispatches.json): Lee to Seddon 8 June p. 868, Lee to Davis 9 June p. 874, Lee to Seddon 13 June p. 886, Lee to Stuart 22 June p. 913, Lee to Davis 23 June p. 924, Lee to Davis 25 June (Williamsport) p. 930 and Pickett to Chilton 21 June p. 910 all exist on those pages with those correspondents and dates. So the references are sound, but the list's description is too narrow: the table is not limited to June, not limited to dispatches to Davis, and the 28 June letter appears only in a note.
items.extraction_notes: Adapter: archive-fulltext (Internet Archive djvu text). The OCR of the table is poor: dates and page numbers come out garbled (for example 'i86j' for 1863, 'Jo' and 'J2^' for digits), so every citation figure must be checked against the scan image before use; the editor's and Palmer's own prose (pp. 148-149 and the note on p. 155) OCRs cleanly. The dispatch texts themselves are in OR vol. 27, already ingested: use this article as a framed index and as a 1900 Lost Cause voice (it argues Lee was starved of men and supplies and thwarted by Richmond), not as a source for the dispatches. Printed pp. 148-155 = leaves 162-169 (1-based); https://archive.org/details/southernhistoric2819sout.
issues: Description is partly inaccurate: it covers March to August 1863 (heading), not only June; it includes Seddon, Cooper, Stuart, Hill, Jenkins and Pickett items, not only Lee to Davis; the 28 June Davis letter is a note, not an entry.
Author (Col. William H. Palmer, formerly chief of staff to A. P. Hill per the editor's note) is missing from the list.
Retrospective, partisan 1900 framing of OR documents; secondary, not a primary source.
The listed Perseus URL cannot be used by a program (robots.txt); catalog_overlap H1:SRC-08 already plans SHSP from the Internet Archive.
Do not allow-list southernhistoric0028rabr (1991 reprint).

items.written: 1863 (Dickinson catalogue date 18 July 1863; clipping masthead The Methodist, New-York; day not visible on the clipping)
items.rights_basis: Underlying text is an 1863 newspaper article (public domain). The only copy is a Dickinson scan; the item page (Wayback capture) carries 'Copyright 2020 Archives & Special Collections at Dickinson College. All rights reserved' and I found no reuse licence on the Dickinson pages I fetched. Counsel or Dickinson should confirm before quoting; a faithful reproduction of a public-domain print adds little, so the risk looks low but is not resolved.
items.evidence: Listed URL: 404 (probe cache, re-read through the client; 301 http to https, then 404). Fetched Wayback capture 20231207203932 of the listed page (200): item 'The Methodist, A Few Days Under Rebel Rule', 11 pages, 18 July 1863, MC 2000.9 B1 F3, gift of Dr. Theodore M. Johnson. Its PDF resolved to capture 20240620182759 (3,555,300 bytes, sha256 19aed028b2b7dfa6d5f0322d5f1e29a44f1247490d563b50aec3b9ef95223174): page 1 is a Dickinson cover sheet (text), pages 2-10 are image-only newspaper column clippings, the last page is the whole clipping with the masthead The Methodist: New-York. I read the images: byline 'By Prof. S. D. Hillman, Carlisle'; he refers to closing the college exercises; sections include The Rebel Entrance into Carlisle, Discussion with Rebel Officers (Majors Pendleton of Ewell's staff and Allen of the topographical corps visit the college libraries and the talk turns to who is winning, with the officers saying all the slave states would be needed and complaining of Union 'stealing' and freeing of their negroes), Appearance of the Rebel Army (Jenkins' cavalry first, a North Carolina regiment, camps on the college grounds), and the shelling. Both checked claims hold: eyewitness account of the occupation and shelling of Carlisle, and a discussion with Confederate officers in which slavery appears as one theme. Mild overstatement: the exchange is chiefly about war aims and success, not slavery alone.
items.extraction_notes: Image-only: no text layer on the clipping pages, so a person must transcribe from the scan (print is clear at 2x) and a second person must check it. Use the single full-clipping page (3 columns visible at the top of the last PDF page; the column strips on pages 2-10 carry the rest). The Dickinson summary and description text are not the author's words. Cite as S. D. summary: Verified 47 listed Part XIII pages (the 31 every-35th entries, n=658+35k, plus 16 targeted: the 10 pages carrying a page-specific note, the 857/858 and 814/873/874 boundary pages, the last entries 1059, and the one plate, p. 673) and the 33 unlisted tail pages 1060-1092 (including the 24 where 61 dispatches begin) against my own fetch of the Internet Archive OCR of OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 3 (djvu text and page_numbers.json hashes equal the historian manifest), plus four page images (pp. 673, 858, 1071, 1077). Findings: (1) every page exists and the printed number sits on IA leaf = page + 6; (2) the index is contiguous 3-1059 but NOT complete: the volume's correspondence runs to p. 1092 (33 pages missing, including the 14-page Union and Confederate Appendix); (3) the Union/Confederate corrected sides are right and the 60 'section transition' labels are false (Union through p. 857, Confederate from p. 858, 536/536 odd-page running heads agree); (4) the template description is accurate in kind on 38 of 47 listed pages I checked; it is wrong for one plate (673), for 17 pages whose window is not 'June 3-Aug 3, 1863' (841-857, Addenda with 1864 and 1878 items), for the 60 hedged labels, and for one page-specific note placed a page too early (445 should be 446); about 51% of pages predate July 1 and only about 7% fall on July 1-3; (5) the registry's per-page dispatch counts come from an older historian dispatches.json than the one now committed. Verdict for all 47 listed pages: APPROVE-LINKOUT-ONLY (tier A1 US Government work, no new text, eHistory links unverifiable because the host blocks bots); the 33 unlisted pages are verified A1 pointers that no entry covers.
systemic_findings: COMPLETENESS. entries.json holds 1,057 Part XIII entries, printed pages 3-1059, each page once, n = page + 655, one link each of the exact shape https://ehistory.osu.edu/books/official-records/045/NNNN, titles 'OR Vol. 27, Part 3, p. N' (script check: 0 irregularities). In the Archive scan (warofrebellion273unit) IA's own page_numbers.json gives leaf = page + 6 for every printed page 4-1241 (only p. 3 has no IA number; its folio '(3)' is printed at the foot), and the printed number is legible on that leaf for 1,179 of 1,238 pages (the rest is OCR garble). The correspondence text runs to p. 1092; p. 1093 begins 'ALTERNATE DESIGNATIONS OF ORGANIZATIONS MENTIONED IN THIS VOLUME' (index matter). So the claim that the page index is complete is only true for 3-1059: it covers 1,057 of 1,090 correspondence pages (97.0%) and omits 33 (1060-1092): the rest of the Army of Northern Virginia organization of July 31 (pp. 1058-1065, the list stops in the middle of it), Confederate returns (1065-1068), Confederate dispatches of Aug 1-5 (1068-1075), a plate (1071), a Jan 1864 Confederate resolution (1075-1076), and an APPENDIX 'documents received too late for insertion in proper sequence' (p. 1077, image-verified): Union appendix pp. 1077-1090 (Gov. Curtin and Gov. Parker, Army of the Potomac orders of June 28-July 3, N. H. Davis's July 2 report of the Second Corps position near Gettysburg, Haupt's July 6 letter to Halleck) and Confederate appendix pp. 1090-1092 (Kemper's brigade itinerary, War Dept circular of July 22). My hand count: about 60 dispatches begin on 22 of those 33 pages (historian index: 61 on 24 pages).

SIDE LABELS. The odd-page running head ('CORRESPONDENCE, ETC. UNION.' or '... CONFEDERATE.') agrees on all 536 odd pages 5-1075 with Union through p. 857 and Confederate from p. 859 (5 garbled heads read by eye). P. 857 is the last Union page (it ends with General Orders No. 41 of Feb 1, 1864); p. 858 opens with the heading 'CONFEDERATE CORRESPONDENCE, ETC.' then Lee to Samuel Jones, June 3 (read in OCR and on the page image n863). So the structural check is confirmed independently: all 60 pages labelled 'Union / Confederate (section transition)' hold one side only (814-857 Union = 44 pages, 858-873 Confederate = 16 pages); no page in 3-1059 mixes sides (even pages have no head, side inferred from neighbours); the registry's corrected side is right and the listed hedge is false. Labels Union for 3-813 and Confederate for 874-1059 are correct. In the 31-page sample 30 labels were right and 1 (p. 843) carried the false hedge.

TEMPLATE ACCURACY (47 listed pages checked: 38 accurate, 8 partly inaccurate, 1 inaccurate). The sentence 'Transcribed page of ... dispatches, orders, telegrams and returns, printed chronologically for June 3-August 3, 1863' is true in kind for most pages and the date window matches the volume title block on p. 3 ('FROM JUNE 3 TO AUGUST 3, 1863'). It fails for: (a) pp. 841-857 (17 pages): enclosures dated Aug 10-18 on 841-842 and, from p. 843 ('ADDENDA.'), Naglee's Sept 28, 1863 report on Norfolk and Portsmouth, a Dec 6, 1878 Meigs letter, Jan-Feb 1864 items and the 1864 resolution of thanks, none chronological and mostly not about Gettysburg; (b) at least 33 pages (3.1%) that hold no dispatch (32 table/roster pages by a heuristic of 40+ lines with 80%+ short lines, plus p. 673, which is a plate of two pen sketches with 82 characters of OCR and no transcribable text; p. 213 is half a statistical table; the current dispatches.json has 74 pages with no row); (c) the 60 hedged side labels; (d) the page-specific notes: 10 pages carry one, 9 are right (586, 679, 808, 923, 941, 1029, 1051, 1058 exactly; 813 incomplete) and 1 is a page early (the Department of the Susquehanna roster of June 30 begins at the foot of p. 446, not 445). 'Gettysburg campaign correspondence' overstates: the volume covers North Carolina, Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Pennsylvania and the Department of the East. By header dates (page boundaries approximate, +/-2): about 543 pages (51%) predate July 1, about 75 (7%) fall on July 1-3 (Union pp. 457-512, Confederate pp. 947-965), about 422 (40%) are July 4-Aug 4, 17 (2%) are addenda. In the 31-page sample: 3 battle-or-battle-adjacent pages, 15 campaign-only, 9 aftermath, 4 tangential (Washington defenses, Norfolk addenda, western Virginia, Petersburg).

STALE REGISTRY COUNTS. qc/structural.json records dispatches.json sha256 50b4f016... (440,262 bytes); the committed historian-src/corpus/or27/dispatches.json is 0240cc36... (475,531 bytes). Per-page 'dispatches_starting_on_page' differs between the two on 212 of 1,057 pages, and 'no dispatch begins on the page' is 74 pages on the current file against 119 in structural.json and QC-REPORT section 5 (examples: p. 3 recorded 0, current 3; p. 913 recorded 0, current 1, and my reading agrees). The late-page figures (61 dispatches on 24 pages after p. 1059) are identical on the current file. My hand count on the 31 sample pages agreed exactly with the current index on 24 and differed by one on 7 (pp. 3, 38, 248, 283, 458, 528, 1018; hand counts are from condensed OCR reading, +/-1). The structural 'pass' for Part XIII checks only index shape and side; it could not see the p. 445 note error, the p. 673 plate, or the 841-857 dating problem.

HISTORIAN CORPUS DEFECTS FOUND ON THE WAY (outside the list; for the verifier workflow). (a) 42 Union Appendix dispatches on pp. 1076-1090 (Curtin, Parker, S. Williams, Butterfield, Meade, Stanton, Haupt) carry side 'confederate' in dispatches.json (44 'confederate' rows on those pages, 2 correct: Kemper's itinerary and the Clay circular). (b) Page cited one too low where a plate or a footer folio intervenes: Elliott, Lee-Imboden and Lee-Wharton are on p. 1051 but indexed 1050; Whiting's indorsement and Pendleton-Early are on p. 1072 (p. 1071 is a plate) but indexed 1071; the Curtin and Parker rows indexed 1076 are on p. 1077 (the Appendix title page prints its folio '(1077)' at the foot, image-verified). (c) The rows on pp. 1065 and 1067 are table headings (a roster date misread '1863-07-81'), not dispatches. (d) On p. 1075 the Lee-Stuart letter of Aug 4 and the undated Lee-Pickett letter are not indexed. (e) The second dispatch on p. 858 is OCR 'June's, 1863'; the page image prints 'June 3'.

LINKS. All 1,057 entries link only to ehistory.osu.edu (serial 045, page = printed page). The pipeline records that host as returning HTTP 403 to automated fetches (owner-confirmed); I did not contact it, so every link target, the serial-45 mapping and eHistory's transcription remain unverified (the QC method checks only link shape). Replacement path from the allowed host: https://archive.org/details/warofrebellion273unit/page/n{page+5}/mode/1up. HTTP HEAD returned 200 for all 80 pages tested (it is a viewer shell, so that proves only that the URL resolves). The index n = page + 5 was verified by viewing page images n678, n863, n1076 and n1082, which show printed folios 673, 858, 1071 and 1077; the other pages rest on the constant offset above. Outside my batch: entry 657 says 1,244 page images, the Archive item has imagecount 1,256 (1,254 leaves in page_numbers.json).

RIGHTS. Tier A1 for every page. Evidence: the Archive OCR front matter prints 'SERIES I - VOLUME XXVII - IN THREE PARTS. PART III - CORRESPONDENCE, ETC. WASHINGTON: GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE 1889'; the HathiTrust catalog API record 000625514 lists item coo.31924077700262, enumcron 'ser.1:v.27:pt.3:Correspondence', rightsCode pd, 'Full view'; the Archive metadata API gives publisher 'Washington : Govt. Print Office'. Both the Archive and HathiTrust carry date 1880 (the series start year), but the volume's own title page says 1889. The 1878 Meigs letter (p. 843) and the 1864 Congressional resolutions (pp. 857, 1075-1076) are also US government documents. The eHistory transcription's own terms were not read (host blocks bots), so the entries are link-out only and any quotation must come from the Archive OCR (djvu text sha256 5bd2aed1..., page_numbers sha256 80f8088e..., both identical to historian manifest). Not verified: nothing about third-party text; I saw none.

No browser was launched; I modified no repo file (scratch files only in the session scratchpad); legacy/ untouched.
